This entry-level AI Engineer will work under close supervision to apply developing technical knowledge in Software Engineering and Generative AI, performing analytic, testing, modeling, and development tasks on smaller projects, and independently on larger, more complex assignments. Perform assigned technical and analytic tasks using established methods and tools, documents methods and results, and escalate novel or ambiguous issues.
Support development of AI-enabled applications and fix straightforward defects under close supervision.
Build and maintain components of LLM-based solutions, including API integrations, prompt and tool/function-calling workflows, and basic RAG pipelines (chunking, embeddings, vector search).
Clean, transform, and analyze data with Python, SQL, and data libraries; build simple ETL steps and visualizations.
Execute assigned test cases, including unit tests and basic retrieval or model evaluations, and help reproduce reported issues.
Serve models and AI services through RESTAPIs and containers, prepare simple configuration changes, and follow deployment runbooks.

Document work and escalation steps in tickets and knowledge base entries.

Problem decomposition, clear communication, reading documentation, collaborating through code review, and explaining results to non-technical people.

APIs and web: requests, REST concepts, FastAPI or Flask to serve models, async basics

Databases SQL (essential): SELECT, WHERE, JOINs, GROUP BY, HAVING, subqueries, CTEs, window functions, indexes, query optimization
Relational databases: PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite; schema design, normalization, primary and foreign keys, transactions
Python connectivity: SQLAlchemy, psycopg2, pandas.read_sql
NoSQL: MongoDB (documents), Redis (caching)
Vector databases (AI-specific): embeddings, similarity search, and tools such as pgvector, Chroma, FAISS, Pinecone
Data pipelines: ETL basics, data warehouses, Airflow concepts
Modern GenAI Skills LLM APIs: Anthropic, OpenAI, structured outputs, tool/function calling
RAG: chunking, embeddings, vector search, retrieval evaluation
Frameworks: LangChain or LlamaIndex (know the basics, but understand what's underneath)
Agents: tool use, multi-step workflows, basic evaluation, and guardrails
MLOps and Deployment Model serving: FastAPI, Docker
Experiment tracking: MLflow, Weights & Biases
Cloud basics: AWS, Azure, or GCP
CI/CD basics, monitoring, model versioning

The primary objective of this position is to lead the volume and sales forecast analytical process for AbbVie's Multiple Myeloma (MM) franchise. The medication is a 100% AbbVie-owned asset, and this role is built to scale with the franchise: beyond the launch indication, the forecast scope is expected to expand across additional oncology medication indications (e.g., earlier lines of therapy) and additional MM pipeline products as they advance toward launch.
Specifically, this position is responsible for developing accurate and timely projections of commercial product volumes for Plan, Update, LBE, LRP, Portfolio, and Actual submissions, as well as providing decision-making support and recommendations to Senior Management. As the MM portfolio grows, the role establishes the forecasting methodology, tools, and cadence that new indications and assets will inherit — making this a franchise-building position, not a single-product one.
The Associate Director builds and maintains deep knowledge of the business through focused partnership with internal AbbVie functions, including Marketing & Sales Management, Marketing Analytics & Business Insights (MABI), Market Access, and Commercial Finance.
Responsibilities:

description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Purpose
This role leads the design and execution of Equity, Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (EEDI) strategies for one of AbbVie's key functions. Reporting to the Director, Programs and Business Partnerships, this individual serves as a strategic driver and takes a hands-on approach — shaping the vision and rolling up their sleeves to make it real. The role partners closely with VP-level leaders, functional EEDI councils, Business HR (BHR), and HR Centers of Excellence (COEs) to deliver measurable business and talent outcomes.
The ideal candidate brings a demonstrated track record of driving organizational impact at scale — someone who combines forward-thinking strategy with a bias for action, and who is equally comfortable setting direction and doing the work. This person operates with both a grounding in proven approaches and a commitment to evolving practices that serve our global, diverse organization.
Responsibilities
Own EEDI functional strategy: Partner with the business to develop the EEDI strategy for assigned function. Lead strategy execution, including roadmap implementation, stakeholder management, communication plans, and achievement of clear measures of success.
Lead and align EEDI councils: Direct the work of EEDI councils by establishing clear goals, aligned priorities, and effective operating models that connect directly to business and EEDI strategy. Facilitate council effectiveness with hands-on engagement through active leadership.
Co-design and manage EEDI programs: Co-design, deliver, and manage EEDI programs that are intentionally inclusive and accessible to all employees. Take ownership of program outcomes, with accountability for adoption and measurable outcomes.
Drive cross-functional alignment: Partner with EEDI leads, BHR and COEs to integrate EEDI principles into foundational people processes and to collaboratively advance new strategies and initiatives — ensuring consistency and coherence across the enterprise.
Embed systemic change in talent processes: Apply change management methodologies to deliver year-over-year progress on key EEDI metrics and overall talent metrics. Ensure aligned and systemic changes across functions, sustained efforts over one-time initiatives.
Serve as a strategic advisor: Advise BHR and COEs on practical, evidence-based ways to embed EEDI into all people and business processes. Provide thought leadership that shapes the HR practices and promotes equitable decision-making — with both global perspective and local sensitivity.
Research and benchmark: Stay up to date on ongoing research and external benchmarking to inform best practices and to identify new opportunities for building a globally inclusive workforce.
Translate data into action: Use AI, workforce data and analytics to identify talent opportunities, assess initiative effectiveness, and establish KPIs that demonstrate measurable business impact. Be a practitioner who understands data and interprets what it means.
Uphold governance standards: Ensure consistent adherence to governance processes and guidelines across all EEDI programming and initiatives.
Education and Experience
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience. Advanced degree or EEDI Certification preferred.
Minimum 8+ years of related EEDI work experience; 5+ years of leadership or high-level consulting roles.
Experience in translating external and internal trends into innovative practices.
Proven track record of facilitating company-level initiatives with multiple stakeholders.
A deep understanding of how to promote EEDI within a large, complex, multi-national organization.
Experience in senior business partnering and advisory roles; ability to build collaborative, business-focused relationships with senior HR and business leaders.
Strong consulting skills, project planning, management and review, with an ability to roll up sleeves to demonstrate initiative and results-orientation, with a focus on service.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, presentation skills, and facilitation skills.
A proactive, resourceful and self-motivated approach to their work.

Serve as executive steward of AbbVie's culture, ensuring priorities are clear, visible, differentiated, measurable, and connected to enterprise outcomes.
Create and execute a multi-year culture amplification roadmap that extends beyond HR processes and activates culture through leadership, organizational systems, business practices, and employee experiences.
Protect what is distinctive and valuable in AbbVie's culture while intentionally evolving the behaviors and ways of working needed for the future.

The EHS Manager is a site-based professional responsible for developing, implementing, and continuously improving environmental, health, safety, and industrial hygiene programs. This role partners with site leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to maintain regulatory and company compliance, reduce risk, improve operational performance, and promote a strong EHS culture.
The successful candidate will bring a solid technical foundation in EHS and/or Industrial Hygiene, preferably with experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, chemical, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments.
Key Responsibilities
EHS Program Leadership
Develop, implement, and continuously improve site EHS programs, management systems, procedures, standards, and training initiatives.
Maintain systems that support legal, regulatory, ethical, and company-policy compliance within the assigned area of responsibility.
Monitor applicable local, regional, national, and global EHS requirements and translate changes into practical site actions.
Support the development and execution of the site EHS strategic plan and long-range improvement roadmap.
Promote a proactive safety culture by identifying opportunities to eliminate hazards, strengthen controls, and improve EHS performance.
Industrial Hygiene
Lead the site Industrial Hygiene program, including the development and execution of exposure-assessment strategies.
Plan, conduct, and manage Industrial Hygiene studies involving chemical, biological, physical, ergonomic, and other workplace hazards, as applicable.
Evaluate exposure-monitoring results and recommend appropriate controls using the hierarchy of controls.
Partner with Occupational Health and other stakeholders on medical-surveillance requirements, employee communication, and follow-up activities, as applicable.
Maintain Industrial Hygiene records, technical reports, assessments, and documentation in accordance with regulatory and company requirements.
Verify the effectiveness of engineering, administrative, and personal protective-equipment controls.
Risk Management and Incident Prevention
Lead or participate in risk assessments, job safety analyses, management-of-change activities, and process-safety reviews, as applicable.
Conduct or coordinate incident investigations, determine root and contributing causes, and develop corrective and preventive actions.
Partner with Engineering, Operations, Quality, Facilities, Maintenance, and other functions to embed EHS requirements into new and modified processes.
Training and Engagement
Develop and deliver EHS and Industrial Hygiene training appropriate to job responsibilities and identified risks.
Promote employee engagement, reporting of hazards and near misses, and continuous improvement.
Performance Management and Communication
Communicate compliance status, significant risks, performance trends, priority issues, and business impacts to key stakeholders.
Prepare clear technical reports, presentations, procedures, and business communications.
Lead or participate in cross-functional teams to deliver EHS objectives and organizational priorities.
Bachelor Degree in Engineering, Science, Business, Industrial Safety, or related/equivalent degree.
At least five (5) years of combined experience managing environmental, health, safety, and sustainability, project management, systems administration programs to assure compliance with government regulations and company policies.
Work experience in implementing EHS regulations, developing programs, conducting incident investigations, EHS metrics, interacting with regulatory agencies and external organizations and managing cross functional teams
Ability to establish measurable project goals and implementation plans, balance conflicting work demands, and develop action plans including the identification of resource requirements. Ability to develop standards and /or policies that meet business objectives. Ability to manage complex data sets and produce usable outputs. Ability to manage responsibilities over a large geographic region
Physical; Walking, sitting and standing. Ability to work with computers, database, and integration of information tracking systems. Fluent in English, both oral and writing.
General knowledge of Quality regulations and standards affecting chemical, biological and medical devices (i.e. Quality Systems and FDA regulations) is desirable. Position requires knowledge on local, state, and OSHA and EPA regulation. General understanding of general industry safety and health standards (NIOSH, ANSI) is required. Understanding of fleet vehicle and/or transportation safety is preferred. Demonstrated data management skills preferred.

title: Engineer, Technology I
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. AbbVie’s Business Technology Solutions (BTS) Information Research (IR) organization is seeking an Engineer, Technology I to help deliver trusted, well-structured, AI-ready data products within ARCH, AbbVie’s R&D Convergence Hub. As part of the DELOS team — Data Exploration and Linked Outcome Solutions — this role helps build the reliable data foundations needed to advance analytics, reporting, knowledge graph capabilities, machine learning, and AI-enabled use cases across R&D.
In this role, you will independently design and develop data pipelines and curated data assets within assigned projects, applying established architecture, engineering patterns, and governance standards. You will collect, integrate, normalize, model, and document research data; implement quality checks; and support publication to the ARCH knowledge graph. Rather than developing AI models directly, you will prepare reliable, accessible, and appropriately governed data for analytics, data science, and AI-enabled use cases.
Working with R&D stakeholders, data scientists, machine learning engineers, platform teams, architects, and data owners, you will translate defined scientific and business requirements into dependable data solutions. You will perform routine and complex engineering tasks independently, understand project objectives and your contribution to them, adapt your approach when needed, and communicate progress, risks, and issues. You will collaborate with internal and contracted engineers on assigned work, seeking guidance on broader architecture decisions and escalating issues outside your scope.
Under the direction of the Associate Director – Data Strategy, AI & Knowledge Enablement, this role contributes to AbbVie’s R&D data transformation by delivering consistent, well-documented data solutions within agreed project scope and timelines. You will learn and apply new methods and technologies to help research partners use trusted data for scientific decision-making.
**This is a hybrid role based in Lake County, IL (Tue, Wed, Thu)
Responsibilities
Data Pipeline & Product Development: Independently design and develop pipelines and curated data assets for assigned scientific or business use cases. Collect, integrate, normalize, model, and transform data from databases, applications, APIs, licensed external sources, and other systems using established engineering patterns.
Reliable Project Delivery: Perform routine and complex engineering tasks competently and independently, producing reliable and consistent results within agreed timelines. Understand broader project objectives, organize assigned work, and adapt your approach when requirements or priorities change.
AI & Knowledge Graph Data Preparation: Clean, standardize, enrich, and structure data and documents for downstream analytics, machine learning, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and knowledge discovery. Organize metadata, support established chunking and embedding workflows, and prepare curated assets for publication to the ARCH knowledge graph.
Data Quality & Technical Documentation: Implement defined data quality checks and maintain technical documentation for pipelines and data assets, including metadata, lineage, transformations, assumptions, and usage guidance. Apply established access, privacy, licensing, and governance requirements.
Collaboration & Progress Communication: Work with scientific, business, engineering, and platform partners to clarify requirements and deliver assigned work. Clearly present project objectives, progress, risks, and issues; collaborate with internal and contracted contributors without responsibility for directing their delivery.
Operations & Method Improvement: Monitor assigned pipelines for performance, freshness, failures, and resource use; troubleshoot and resolve issues within your scope and escalate when needed. Learn and implement new methods and technologies and contribute to reusable patterns and automation with guidance as appropriate.
Compliance & Standards: Understand and adhere to applicable Corporate and Divisional policies, including code of conduct, safety, GxP compliance, data security, data governance, relevant regulatory or contractual requirements, and the software development lifecycle.
Bachelor’s Degree in Information Technology, Data Engineering, Computer Science, Informatics, Life Sciences, or a related field plus 4 years of experience; Master’s Degree plus 2 years of experience.
Practical experience developing data pipelines or data solutions using SQL, Python, and ETL/ELT patterns, with knowledge of workflow orchestration tools such as Airflow.
Theoretical and practical knowledge of data integration, data modeling, data storage, and modern data platforms sufficient to independently complete routine and complex engineering tasks within established standards.
Experience cleaning, standardizing, transforming, and documenting data for analytics or scientific use, including applying data quality checks and organizing metadata.
Ability to organize assigned work, multitask, meet timelines, understand project objectives, adapt your approach when needed, and learn and apply new methods and technologies.
Strong written and oral English communication skills, with the ability to explain technical work, present project objectives and progress, and collaborate with scientific, business, and technical partners.
Hands-on data engineering: develop reusable, well-structured data assets for defined analytics and AI-enabled use cases.
Data quality and documentation: apply established metadata, lineage, governance, and appropriate-use practices to assigned data assets.
Technical problem-solving: apply practical knowledge of data platforms, pipelines, integration, and orchestration; learn and implement new tools and methods.
Work planning and operational discipline: organize concurrent assignments, monitor pipelines, troubleshoot issues, meet timelines, and escalate risks when needed.
Team collaboration: clarify requirements, share technical knowledge, and work effectively with internal and external contributors on assigned project tasks.
Clear communication: explain technical concepts and present project objectives, progress, risks, and dependencies to scientific, business, and technical audiences.
Preferred
Pharmaceutical, healthcare, or life sciences industry experience, particularly with research, discovery, translational, clinical, or scientific data.
Familiarity with knowledge graphs, graph databases, ontology-based structures, semantic data, or linked-data concepts.
Exposure to cloud or modern data platform technologies such as AWS, Databricks, Spark, Snowflake, or Neo4j, and to Agile delivery practices or tools such as Jira.
Exposure to data preparation for machine learning, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), embeddings, or vector search, and familiarity with governance, security, privacy, licensing, or documentation in regulated data environments.

The Facility Planner serves as a key figure in optimizing the use of an organization's physical spaces, ensuring they are both effective and efficient. Building and maintaining strong relationships with various business units and a diverse range of stakeholders to align organizational goals is key. By partnering with leadership, they develop strategic plans to reorganize groups, optimizing spaces to address the specific needs of different business units. Essential to the role is the enforcement of design standards, which ensures a consistent and functional environment across the organization. Reviews and manages service requests for renovations, handling projects from minor upgrades to large-scale transformations. Leading front-end planning efforts, the planner identifies space requirements early on and sets the scope. This proactive approach ensures that projects align with business objectives and are executed smoothly.
Responsibilities
Foster strong stakeholder relationships through proactive communication and collaboration, aligning goals with company values while maintaining transparency and recognizing contributions.
Gather and analyze data on space utilization, occupancy, and facility conditions to support informed strategic planning and initiatives. Understand data requirements by collaborating with the CAFM (Computer-Aided Facility Management) team to establish clear data quality standards and objectives. Implement facility planning policies, procedures, and standards that ensure compliance with regulations and organizational values, while advocating change management initiatives to support workplace efficiency and innovation.

Proficiency in the MS Office Suite, including advanced skills in MS Excel.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities.

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. Purpose :
The Global Connected Logistics and Internet of Things (IoT) Strategy Lead shapes and advances enterprise capabilities that improve visibility, product protection, sustainability and operational performance across the global distribution and logistics network.
This individual contributor role connects business strategy with practical implementation. The individual will lead global initiatives, coordinate requirements and interdependencies across global functions and regions, and partner with Business Technology Solutions (BTS), external providers and operational teams to deploy solutions that are scalable, viable and fit for purpose. There is a travel element to this role, with business meetings in US and Europe, primarily but not limited to those regions.
The successful candidate will bring a combination of strategic thinking, program leadership, commercial and vendor management, and strong cross-functional influence. The position is designed for an experienced supply chain, logistics, technology-enabled transformation professional and does not require deep engineering expertise in every device or platform.
Responsibilities:
Own and continuously develop AbbVie's global connected logistics strategy and multi-year roadmap. This covers shipment visibility, temperature monitoring, RFID, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), geolocation and other monitoring technologies, with the goal of improving product protection, risk management and operational decision-making.
Lead the assessment of emerging logistics technologies and monitoring solutions. Work with regional and functional teams to decide which capabilities to pilot, scale globally, integrate into existing processes or phase out, based on business value and operational fit. Lead priority device and IoT initiatives from opportunity definition through implementation, coordinating requirements, milestones, risks and dependencies to speed up deployment and deliver measurable business value.
Partner with Business Technology Solutions (BTS) and technology partners to turn business requirements into functional, data and integration requirements. Make sure solutions are scalable, supportable and compliant with Good Distribution Practice (GDP).

Implement risk-based security standards and solutions (e.g., TAPA). Lead cross-functional initiatives that improve product security, including programs that make high-value products less visible during transportation and distribution. Together, these reduce theft, diversion and other supply chain risks and strengthen supply chain resilience.
Evolve the working relationship with EH&S on distribution and logistics sustainability. Support Scope 3 emissions guidance, governance and training for emissions self-reporting across markets and third-party partners, and coordinate Product Carbon Footprint requests, to improve data consistency, adoption and alignment with standards.
Engage Distribution Managers, Regional Transportation Management teams and senior cross-functional leaders to address partner performance. Embed requirements, risks and interdependencies into functional, regional and enterprise strategies, enabling clear accountability and timely decisions.

A minimum of eight years of progressive experience in supply chain, distribution, logistics, technology-enabled transformation, program management, sustainability, security or a related discipline. Experience in pharmaceuticals, life sciences or another regulated industry is preferred but not required.
Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from strategy through implementation in a global or multi-regional environment.
Experience with one or more of the following areas is preferred: shipment visibility, temperature monitoring, connected devices, IoT, telematics, product or freight security, logistics sustainability, carbon reporting, or vendor-managed technology solutions.
Ability to translate business needs into clear requirements and partner effectively with technology teams on data, integration, system and architecture considerations without requiring hands-on engineering ownership.
Experience managing external vendors, logistics providers or strategic partners, including performance management, governance and issue resolution.
Strong stakeholder leadership and influencing skills, with the ability to build alignment across senior leaders, regional teams, functional experts and external partners without direct authority.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex information into concise, executive-ready recommendations and updates.

Global Lab Solutions (GLS), part of Operations Quality Assurance, designs and enables the systems, capabilities, standards, and partnerships that strengthen laboratory performance, support pipeline progression, and promote consistent, compliant execution across AbbVie’s global Quality Control network. Within GLS, Global QC Product Governance translates product and analytical strategy into QC readiness by connecting R&D, Product Development Science & Technology (PDS&T), Operations Quality, and QC laboratories to ensure analytical methods, standards, critical reagents, and supporting controls are ready for reliable commercial execution. AbbVie is seeking an accomplished scientific and Quality leader for the role of Global QC Product Lead. This individual will provide strategic Quality leadership and governance for the implementation and lifecycle management of commercial analytical methods across AbbVie’s global QC network. Serving as a primary Global QC interface for assigned products, the Product Lead will integrate scientific, Quality, operational, and product considerations to enable analytical strategies that are compliant, fit for routine use, transferable, and sustainable.
The role provides independent oversight and decision-making for QC analytical implementation, including review and challenge of validation, co-validation, and method transfer strategies; assessment of laboratory capability and readiness; and determination of the QC method design needed for dependable commercial execution. The Customer Logistics Planner is the execution and control hub for outbound shipments in the Gaucho third-party manufacturing model. The role coordinates end-to-end order and shipment execution from second-leg stock transport order creation through shipment departure, documentation archiving, exception resolution and stakeholder communication.
The planner helps protect supply continuity and customer service by maintaining accurate system transactions, compliant shipping documentation, timely visibility and early escalation of risks.
The Customer Logistics Planner owns shipment execution and visibility within the Shipment CoE, while Transportation retains ownership of carrier strategy, transportation procurement and carrier management.
Key responsibilities
Order and delivery execution: Create and manage second-leg STOs and outbound deliveries in SAP; update weights and measurements using the Nota Fiscal; create packing lists; post goods issue for departed shipments; and provide accurate shipment data to support commercial invoicing.
Shipping and export documentation: Prepare pro forma invoices and other shipment documentation for customs and payment purposes; check completeness and compliance; and archive final shipping documentation in the designated repository.
Shipment control and visibility: Maintain shipping forecasts and master arrival schedules, monitor open orders and deliveries, review allocation issues and blocks, and escalate overdue or at-risk shipments.
Exception management: Coordinate resolution of shipment delays, booking constraints, documentation gaps, complaints, discrepancies, complex lane requirements and urgent business requests, working with Transportation and other relevant functions as needed.
Stakeholder coordination: Coordinate daily with the third-party manufacturer, Global Supply Planning, Transportation, affiliates, Global Trade Compliance, Finance, Quality, Planning and other supply chain partners. Engage with carriers as required in line with the agreed Transportation interface and operating model.
Affiliate and customer service: Provide timely updates and pre-alert information, align around holiday schedules and market-specific requirements, and support affiliates with complex export and transportation needs.
Performance and governance: Support operational and carrier performance reviews by providing shipment data, issue trends and execution insights, together with KPI reporting, month-end activities, audit readiness, process controls and the Calendar of Discipline.
Continuous improvement: Identify process gaps, improve standard work, strengthen controls and visibility, and contribute to scalable solutions as shipment volumes and regional complexity increase. Support stabilization and continuous improvement of new operating models as processes and interfaces mature.
Key interfaces
Internal: Shipment CoE, Transportation, Global Supply Planning, Finance, Global Trade Compliance, Quality Assurance, Planning, manufacturing and distribution teams, and commercial affiliates.
External: Third-party manufacturer, freight forwarders, service providers, destination-market partners and carriers, with carrier engagement coordinated through Transportation where applicable.
Bachelor's or master's degree, preferably in Logistics, Supply Chain, Operations, Business Management, or a related discipline.
Minimum three years of relevant experience in logistics, customer logistics, order management, supply chain execution, or a comparable environment.
Hands-on ERP experience, preferably SAP, including order, delivery, shipment, or inventory transactions.
Experience with international shipping documentation, export processes, customs-related requirements, and cross-functional stakeholder coordination.
Fluent written and spoken English; additional languages are an advantage for international market support.

AbbVie’s Global Forecasting Center of Excellence sets forecasting standards and builds the analytical capabilities that guide enterprise planning. Ability to translate business context into modeling decisions and communicate technical results clearly to non-technical audiences.
Strong documentation skills and the ability to manage multiple workstreams in a matrixed environment.

Experience in pharmaceutical, biotech, or life sciences commercial analytics, forecasting, or data science.
Experience with commercial volume forecasting and pharmaceutical data sources (e.g., prescription, patient flow, and epidemiology data).
Experience integrating models into business processes with defined planning cycles, and familiarity with enterprise forecasting platforms.
Exposure to large language models and generative AI in analytical contexts.
Experience with model governance frameworks, including documentation, validation, and responsible-use guidelines.

Purpose:
This position reports into the Clinical Sciences (CS) Product Office in the CS Strategic Operations organization. The CS Product Office works collaboratively and strategically with colleagues across the product lifecycle to identify, evaluate, understand and communicate the safety profile of our drugs to protect patients worldwide.
The Product Safety Team Project Management group (PST PM) plays a critical role in shaping and driving the strategic priorities of the PST through providing exceptional and strategic project management leadership. The PST is a high-profile, high-impact team that leads and owns safety decisions and strategy across the product lifecycle. The team partners with stakeholders across the product lifecycle to provide innovative safety-driven strategies, which will maximize product benefit-risk for patients.
Responsibilities:
In partnership with PST Lead, shape the PST strategic priorities and drive implementation by applying strong understanding of the Therapeutic Area, regulatory requirements, signal management & project management to influence characterization of the compound/product safety & effectiveness profile. This responsibility will be accomplished through building a strong and trusted relationship with the PST Lead and core team members.
In partnership with the PST Lead, manage multiple Product Safety Teams across multiple Therapeutic Areas. This includes meeting planning and facilitation, meeting minute documentation and post-meeting/general team management activities. Increase meeting productivity and advance decision-making effectively through the application of strong skillsets in influencing, leadership, relationship building, proactive-ness, curiosity, active engagement and developing strategic thinking.
Proactively utilize experience and knowledge to support the PST Lead in framing safety issues and making decisions. Anticipate possible outcomes of safety issues and provide guidance to the PST Lead so that he/she can be proactively prepared. Systematically analyze the impact of safety decisions and connect the dots across other decisions, discussions, and actions. Communicate perspectives to PST Lead and collaborate with other PST PMs and the PST Lead on solutions.
In partnership with PST Lead, manage escalation of safety issues and decisions to management and Safety Review Board (SRB). Create escalation documentation (e. g. SRB presentations) and help prepare the PST Leads for discussions. Manage the close-out of SRB action items for assigned PSTs.
Support the PST Lead in strengthening internal partnership/influence and establishing their role as the company leader of safety issues related to their compounds/products. Identify new opportunities for the PST Lead to build relationships and present thought leadership to peers.
Support the PST Lead in strengthening external engagement/presence by providing recommendations on channels for expanding external engagement including topic ideas for publications, conferences to present at key industry relationships to develop, etc. Support the creation of content for external engagement activities.
Drive timely development of key PST deliverables by planning and facilitating productive working sessions to create deliverables; share perspectives; push the thinking to create robust deliverables, suggest improvements, and connect the dots.
Support inspection /audit readiness activities. Engage in supporting PST-related inspection/audit activities and CAPAs/commitments.
BA/BS/MA/MS (nursing or pharmacy, biologic/medical science, or healthcare professional preferred), with 3+ years clinical or pharmaceutical industry experience (advanced degree is preferred)
Experience in one of the following areas is preferred: clinical operations management, clinical study management, drug development, risk management, and/or drug safety operations
At least 3 years hands-on project management experience in leading cross-functional projects within a global company, including hands-on experience applying project management tools and templates.
Effective verbal and written communication skills. Should be able to adapt communication style to suit different audiences.
Effective facilitation skills. Must be able to facilitate group discussions.
Ability to work independently, influence stakeholders, and present sound business strategies.
Ability to demonstrate effectiveness in working in a multidisciplinary, matrix team situation.

Directs renovation and infrastructure programs through site leadership, aligning scope, sequencing, and constraints to portfolio priorities.
Drives consistent execution of safety and regulatory requirements for facilities work, ensuring risks, findings, and corrective actions are addressed to closure.
Develops site leaders and engineers by reinforcing disciplined planning routines, stakeholder alignment cadence, and traceable decision and action documentation.
Responsible for leading and optimizing operational aspects across teams, as well as implementing workforce and succession plans to meet business needs.

Deliver the Durham campus infrastructure portfolio
1. Lead infrastructure projects—including campus development, utilities, the Spine, warehouse, laboratory, administrative, office, and support buildings—from planning through design, construction, commissioning, and handover. Balance campus priorities and coordinate interfaces and dependencies across infrastructure projects and adjacent scopes. title: Project Manager
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
New to North Carolina. Known for pursuing breakthroughs in medicine.
Ready to join our team?
At AbbVie, we bring together talented people and innovative science to develop medicines that help patients. Now, we’re bringing that commitment to Durham, North Carolina, with a new manufacturing campus that will expand our ability to produce medicines and create opportunities in the Research Triangle.
The campus will integrate advanced manufacturing, laboratory technologies and AI to support the production of immunology, oncology and neuroscience medicines. The first phase will include manufacturing facilities, next-generation laboratories, a warehouse, administrative offices and employee wellness facilities.
To learn more about this investment, please visit https://www.abbvie.com/abbvie-north-carolina-manufacturing.html
We are now recruiting our  Project Manager as part of the core start up leadership team . In this role, you will responsible for planning, designing, and delivering engineering projects that support manufacturing, R&D, and infrastructure needs. You will lead cross-functional efforts to implement new systems, equipment, and technologies while ensuring compliance with quality, safety, and regulatory standards. You will manage project scope, schedule, and budget to deliver operational improvements and business value.
Key Responsibilities
As Project Manager , you will lead technical workstreams and contribute to program outcomes by developing actionable methods and analyses, collaborate with cross‑functional partners to integrate technical solutions throughout the lifecycle, and advise on complex technical decisions and risks. You will:
Define project design and engineering planning for assigned projects.
Lead system, equipment, and technology installations, ensuring safe integration, commissioning readiness, and on-time delivery.
Assess project processes and resolves operational or technical issues.
Deliver operational improvements, business value delivery, and site production efficiency through effective project execution.
Provide technical guidance to junior engineers and collaborate with cross-functional teams, ensuring integration of systems, equipment, andtechnologies.
Deliver high‑quality technical outputs for complex projects and programs; defines and validates methods, documents results and keyassumptions, ensures adherence to applicable standards and controls, and communicates technical progress, impacts and recommendedmitigations to project leads and stakeholders
You will have in-depth knowledge typically obtained through advanced education and experience; with a Bachelors degree in Engineering or similiar related discipline and 8 + years relevant industry experience.
Experience in drug substance, drug product, biologics and/or aseptic sterile fill finish is required
Project Management experience is required with specific experience in start up is preferred (PMP certification is preferred)
You will have demonstrated your ability to partner cross functionally with successful teams in a GMP manufacturing environment
Travel up to 50% during the initial start up phase of the project

title: Scientist, Systems Immunology
description:

AbbVie Immunology is expanding its discovery Systems Immunology team in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The team is focused on identifying new targets for the treatment of autoimmune and chronic inflammatory diseases through computational analysis of human disease tissue-derived datasets and validating targets using humanized experimental approaches.
We are seeking a highly motivated and skilled individual to join our team as a Computational Immunology Scientist. The successful candidate will develop and implement computational approaches to understand disease biology and drug responses using high-throughput molecular profiling data. This role will involve integrating single-cell RNA-seq, scATAC-seq, TCR/BCR repertoire, bulk RNA-seq, and Olink proteomics data to characterize disease-associated cell states, investigate gene regulatory networks, and identify therapeutic opportunities.
The scientist will work in a multidisciplinary team analyzing multiomics datasets to derive insights into immunological diseases and identify novel therapeutic targets relevant to patient cohorts and AbbVie pipeline drugs. The candidate will also contribute to scientific conference presentations, peer-reviewed publications of translational findings, new drug applications, and regulatory filings. If you are passionate about translating complex biological data into actionable insights and advancing personalized medicine, we encourage you to apply.
This position will be based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and requires passion, attention to detail, prior hands-on experience, and teamwork.
Key Responsibilities:
Analyze scRNA-seq, and CITE-seq, datasets, including quality control, integration, clustering, and cell-type and cell-state annotation.
Integrate patient cohorts with reference atlases and perform differential expression, abundance, and pathway analyses, accounting for donor variation and study design.
Analyze scATAC-seq data to identify differential accessibility, transcription factor motifs, and candidate regulatory programs; integrate accessibility with gene expression to infer peak-to-gene relationships.
Analyze TCR/BCR repertoires, including clonotype assignment, clonal expansion, diversity, V(D)J usage, and sharing across tissues or time points; link clonotypes to matched single-cell profiles.
Analyze bulk RNA-seq and Olink proteomics data and integrate multiomics findings to support target prioritization and biomarker hypotheses; maintain documented, version-controlled workflows and evaluate methods using cloud or high-performance computing.
Collaborate with internal and external scientists to prioritize hypotheses for validation, communicate findings and limitations, and contribute to presentations and publications.
BS or MS degree in computational biology, bioinformatics, genomics, biostatistics, computer science, or a related quantitative field with typically 5-7+ years (BS) or 2-5+ years (MS) of relevant experience.
Hands-on scRNA-seq analysis experience or experience with scATAC-seq or TCR/BCR analysis, with interest in developing expertise across both.
Proficiency in Python and/or R and experience working in Linux-based computing environments.
Experience with commonly used bioinformatics tools and frameworks such as Scanpy, AnnData, Cell Ranger, scvi-tools, DESeq2, GSEA, WGCNA, or related methods.
Working knowledge of statistical analysis, multiple-testing correction, batch effects, and biological replication in high-dimensional datasets.
Ability to translate biological questions into analyses, interpret and communicate results critically, collaborate effectively, and manage multiple priorities with attention to detail.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively, manage multiple priorities, and deliver high-quality analyses with attention to detail.
Preferred Qualifications:
Experience analyzing Olink or other high-plex proteomics datasets.
Experience with CITE-seq, ATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomics, or integrative multi-omics analysis.
Experience building or benchmarking machine-learning models, including convolutional neural networks, autoencoders, generative models, transfer learning, or foundation models.
Experience with cloud or high-performance computing, including AWS and/or SLURM.
Understanding of immunology and inflammatory disease biology; experience supporting target discovery with experimental teams and communicating research through presentations, publications, or reports.
Evidence of scientific communication through presentations, posters, publications, technical reports, or related research contributions.

Reporting to the VP of Operations AI and Digital Transformation, this role sets the multi-year digital vision, architecture principles, and investment roadmap that connect Industry 4.0/5.0 capabilities, data and AI platforms, and site-level execution to measurable business value. The Sr. Director serves as a senior digital voice of Operations with the Operations Leadership Team, Business Technology Solutions (BTS), and enterprise governance forums, ensuring Operations is positioned as an industry leader in digitally enabled, compliant, and resilient manufacturing and supply.
Strategy and Roadmap
Digital vision and strategy: Define and own the 3-to-5-year Operations digital strategy and target-state architecture across Supply Chain, Quality/QC, PDS&T, Engineering, and Security, aligned to enterprise, Operations, and AI strategies.
Integrated roadmap: Translate strategy into a prioritized, sequenced, and funded roadmap (including LRP resource and investment planning) that balances near-term value capture with long-term capability building.
Technology foresight: Scan, benchmark, and assess emerging technologies (e.g., connected worker, digital twins, MES/MOM, autonomous operations, GenAI/agentic AI, robotics, advanced analytics) against industry peers and recommend adoption pathways.

Standards and platforms: Establish common digital standards, reference architectures, and data foundations (e.g., shopfloor integration layer, unified namespace, data products) that enable reuse and scale across sites and functions and avoid duplicative solutions.
Governance and compliance: Chair or co-lead digital governance and technology review forums with BTS, Quality, and Security; ensure GxP/data integrity, computer system assurance, cybersecurity (IT/OT), and regulatory expectations are built into every digital initiative.

Portfolio value management: Define business cases, KPIs, and benefit-tracking for the digital portfolio (e.g., yield, right-first-time, cycle time, inventory, deviations, labor productivity, EHS) and report realized value to the Ops Leadership Team and Finance.
Scaled deployment: Partner with functional leaders, site leadership, BTS, and Global Engineering & Automation to move proven pilots to standardized, multi-site deployment with clear ownership and adoption plans.
Partner ecosystem: Develop strategic relationships with technology vendors, startups, academia, and industry consortia; shape sourcing strategy with Procurement.
Leadership and Change
Organization and culture: Build and lead a high-performing digital strategy, architecture, and portfolio team; develop talent, digital fluency, and a continuous improvement and innovation culture across Operations.
Executive engagement: Represent Operations Digital Strategy in enterprise forums (e.g., Enterprise AI SteerCo), communicating progress, risks, and investment needs to senior executives
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Science, Computer Science, or a related technical field required; Master’s or MBA preferred.
Minimum of 15–18 years of experience in biopharmaceutical, pharmaceutical, or regulated manufacturing operations, digital, or technology roles, including 8+ years leading enterprise-scale digital strategy or transformation in a senior leadership capacity.
Proven track record of setting multi-year digital roadmaps and delivering scaled, measurable value across multiple sites and functions (manufacturing, supply chain, quality/QC, engineering, PDS&T).
Deep understanding of Industry 4.0/5.0 and digital manufacturing technologies (MES/MOM, IIoT, data platforms, digital twins, advanced process control, robotics/automation, AI/ML and GenAI) and their application in GxP environments.
Working knowledge of GxP/GMP, data integrity (ALCOA+), computer system assurance, and OT/IT cybersecurity expectations for pharma operations.
Experience establishing digital governance, architecture standards, and investment/benefit-management frameworks in partnership with IT/BTS and Finance.
Demonstrated executive presence and ability to influence senior leaders, build coalitions, and navigate a complex global matrix organization.
Strong change leadership skills, with experience driving adoption of new technologies and ways of working at scale.
Experience building and developing leaders and multidisciplinary teams; consulting or external technology-partner experience is a plus.
Excellent strategic thinking, communication, and storytelling skills, with the ability to translate complex technology concepts into business outcomes.

Establish specifications and technical requirements for major electrical equipment and support technical bid evaluations/vendor reviews.

Monitor event conditions and adjust plans in response to changing risks, schedules, attendance, or operational needs.
Document incidents, observations, and after-action findings; recommend improvements for future events.

Experience in pharmaceutical, life-sciences, healthcare, manufacturing, law enforcement, or another regulated operating environment.

Experience planning events at facilities with controlled access, restricted areas, or sensitive operations.

General Position Summary/Purpose:
The Market Access and Patient Services Insights (MAPS) organization within APEX plays an instrumental role in shaping market access strategies for all of AbbVie’s US brands. As a member of this team, you will lead the planning and execution of primary/ secondary market research to identify payer opportunities and threats, influence the development of market access strategies and tactics, enable organizational learning, and ensure alignment of insights with the broader commercial goals of each brand.  This is a hybrid role with the focus on Primary Market Research with an opportunity for some data analytics.
The role requires strong research experience as well as subject matter expertise within the overall U.S. market access environment. The role provides insights that directly impact patient and physician access to AbbVie brands through its influence on the development of pricing, contracting, messaging and other access strategies.
Key Accountabilities/Core Job Responsibilities:
Lead primary and secondary market research activities on a key oncology brand and/or launch indications that influence market access through fact-based analysis, customer insights and business knowledge. Co-develop with U.S. Market Access commercial leaders, innovative Pricing and Contracting strategies to achieve optimal payer formulary access that maximize net sales for assigned brands. Deliver customer insights through market research, competitive simulation, and customer/environmental modeling to understand complex economic and clinical dynamics that drive payer access and shape brand demand. Demonstrate strong understanding of the U.S. healthcare landscape and key AbbVie therapeutic areas to identify and proactively address opportunities and threats. Build collaborative relationships with internal U.S. Market Access Sales and Marketing stakeholders. Align insights to Brand insight partners, that when integrated with HCP and Consumer insights, positively impacts brand decision making.
Key areas of functional scope include:
Leading the creative process for developing GPO, IDN, Specialty Pharmacy, Health Plan and PBM go-to-market strategies for launch brands across payer channels and conveying analytical narratives that describe the market environment influencing stakeholder negotiations.
Leading the delivery of brand specific market access insights and response to specific market access issues/ trends. Areas of depth include gross/net pricing, contracting strategy, value proposition development, implications of competitive launches on access, investigative analytics related to market events and competitive actions, strategies for payer formulary coverage and reimbursement, and identifying value drivers that guide clinical data development and value positioning.
Demonstrating a strong understanding of both primary/ secondary research methodologies and the ability to synthesize insights into compelling narratives. Responsible for leading the communication of market access insights to leadership requiring a broad range of market access expertise as these brands commonly experience differing market access challenges.

11 years of professional experience

description:
About Allergan Aesthetics
At Allergan Aesthetics, an AbbVie company, we develop, manufacture, and market a portfolio of leading aesthetics brands and products. Our aesthetics portfolio includes facial injectables, body contouring, plastics, skin care, and more. Our goal is to consistently provide our customers with innovation, education, exceptional service, and a commitment to excellence, all with a personal touch. For more information, visit https://global.allerganaesthetics.com/. Follow Allergan Aesthetics on LinkedIn.
This is a hybrid role including in office and remote working days. Must be a resident or relocatable to Austin TX area.
Must be able to work one of the below shifts:
8:00am-4:30pm CT, or 8:30-5:00pmCT, 7:30-4:30pmCT or 8:00-5pmCT
The Sr Inside Sales Business Development Manager is a revenue generating position with responsibility for quarterly sales quota attainment for the Facial Aesthetics portfolio of products (BOTOX® Cosmetic, JUVÉDERM® Collection of Fillers, SkinMedica®, KYBELLA®) and for managing and enhancing portfolio growth through business development activities using primarily phone communication.
The Sr IBDM represents the Allergan Aesthetics product portfolio to targeted aesthetic customers within a designated geographical area. Responsible for product and program education, product adoption, and portfolio growth through business development activities.
The Sr IBDM provides technical product and procedure training, as well as competitive product differentiation.  Assigned sales goals are obtained through strategic analysis of account data, strong knowledge of accounts aesthetic goals, understanding of market dynamics, application of consultative selling and implementation of the U.S. Sales/Marketing plan.  The company offers flexible career paths with a strong emphasis on opportunity for internal mobility.
Allergan Sr IBDMs must:
Leverage Allergan Medical resources to enhance adoption of the Allergan Medical Aesthetics Portfolio.  Synergistically work and coordinate activities with other Allergan sales personnel and support teams (include, but are not limited to, Facial Aesthetics, CoolSculpting®, SkinMedica®, and Marketing).  Complies with required reports, requests, and compliance policies.
Key Duties and Responsibilities:
Consistently achieves sales quota across portfolio. Proficient in sales execution component of marketing plans. Independently creates call and business development plans across the product portfolio. Demonstrates adaptability and creativity with multiple initiatives.
Sales processes must be focused toward business growth and relationship building.
Manages attainment of assigned sales quota and customer satisfaction through consistent communication with the Regional Manager and Inside Sales Area Manager, managing own sample allocation, placing orders, providing marketing materials, and assisting accounts with marketing strategies.   Also leads execution on all campaigns/promotions, new product launches, training of accounts on Allergan programs and other sales related initiatives.
Develop product knowledge and utilize to best serve customer’s current business needs, as well as to prospect new products, program, and training opportunities with current accounts and to identify and qualify new business. Educate the customer regarding indications, contraindications, and safety of the products, and how they fulfill the needs of the customer. Obtain information needed to accurately understand problems and use this information to determine solutions and formulate new and innovative ideas proactively solve customer problems in a manner that exceeds customer expectations.
Identifying growth opportunities to include: expanding reach with customer base, expanding product portfolio utilization with existing accounts, and launching new products and new product indications.
Educating and supporting the customer with marketing strategies including but not limited to website and social media development, internal office branding, patient segmentation, and external marketing strategies.
Pre-planning sales calls and maintaining efficient time management skills to ensure maximum customer contact and highest level of customer engagement.
Maintaining updated knowledge of the industry and competitive products.
Maintaining compliance with all applicable quality and regulatory guidelines as an integral part of business operations.
Collaboration with Regional Manager, respective field reps and Inside Sales Area Manager - Work cross- functionally with field sales in order to drive sales objectives, cultivate relationships, and collaborate on growth opportunities.
Leave of absence and vacant territory coverage includes collaboration with the respective Sales Representative, Region Manager, and Inside Sales Area Manager to develop and negotiate a coverage plan.   This can include consistent communication- managing own sample allocation, placing orders, providing marketing materials, and assisting accounts with marketing and business development strategies.   Also includes execution on all campaigns/promotions, new product launches and other sales related initiatives.
Attend sales training and sales meetings as required.
Complete administrative responsibilities such as: on a timely basis, to include presentations, expense reports, etc.
Demonstrate a strong work ethic and represent the Company with high integrity, ethics, honesty, loyalty, and professionalism at all times
Education and Experience:
Bachelor's degree preferred or relevant and equivalent industry experience required.
Requirements:
Two or more years of relevant sales experience is required.
A track record of earning strong commissions, the ability to work independently, be highly organized and exhibit superior communication skills required.
Ability to travel by air and/or car up to 15-20% of the time.

Experience in the aesthetics/healthcare industry involving interaction with physicians, patients, etc.
Experience in educating or influencing targeted customers.
Two years of working in Inside Sales preferred.

Positive role model.

title: 2027 University Graduate - Enterprise Architecture Analyst
description:
2027 University Graduate - Enterprise Architecture Analyst (Open)
The Opportunity
At Adobe, our mission is to empower creatives, marketers, and IT professionals with application-based products that transform their daily work and accelerate progress towards their business goals. Our Technical Pre-Sales (TPS) organization plays a critical role in preparing customers to purchase Adobe’s integrated solutions by understanding their business needs, defining and validating their technical requirements, and demonstrating their ideal future state with Adobe technology.
The Enterprise Architecture (EA) team is within the TPS group. This role will be supporting the Enterprise Architecture (EA) team within TPS.
Learn More about Enterprise Architecture
Adobe’s Enterprise Architecture team sits within the TPS organization and works directly with Adobe customers to understand their current technology architecture and usage, evaluate its effectiveness as it relates to their larger business objectives, and create a future-state technology architecture to best support their long-term marketing vision.
You will learn how the team runs, how they interact with customers, real-world customer problems mapped to Adobe software solutions, and what key results they are responsible for building all while supporting and influencing the growing team’s operational strategy.
What You’ll Do
Learn to connect the dots between customers’ business problems and Adobe’s solution offerings to demonstrate value for our customers and their business
Collaborate with cross-organizational partners including sales teams, solution experts, digital strategists, customer success managers, and more to develop innovative solutions to help them through various stages in the sales cycle
Gain experience with conducting current-state technology analyses and developing high-impact recommendations for future-state technology
Learn to build custom architecture diagrams and phased implementations that showcase how Adobe technology can best support our customers’ objectives
Create presentations to best communicate technical information and architecture mapping to our customers’ business needs
Leverage Agentic AI technologies to enhance our current offerings and help to design the future for our customers’ evolving digital landscapes
Help brands fully capitalize on the era of digital & agentic transformation, so they can deliver personalized and meaningful experiences across all devices and channels for their customers by aligning to Adobe Customer Experience Orchestration solutions.
What You Need to Succeed
Currently enrolled full time and pursuing a Bachelor's degree graduating between December 2026 and June 2027
Proven interest in business strategy, digital marketing, technology, analytics or experience design through coursework, extracurricular activities, or work/internship experience
Curiosity and/or application across agentic AI technologies, including agents, LLMs and AI tooling
Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills including conducting research, developing hypotheses, and synthesizing recommendations
Strong interpersonal skills with ability to work effectively with people at all levels in an organization
Ability to communicate complex ideas optimally both verbally and in writing; ability to deliver compelling customer presentations communicating technical concepts
Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment
Passion for new knowledge, resourceful and able to absorb concepts quickly
You enjoy challenges and learning about industry and technology trends
You bring a positive, can-do attitude to your work

Adobe empowers everyone to create through innovative platforms and tools that unleash creativity, productivity and personalized customer experiences. Adobe’s industry-leading offerings including Adobe Acrobat Studio, Adobe Express, Adobe Firefly, Creative Cloud, Adobe Experience Platform, Adobe Experience Manager, and GenStudio enable people and businesses to turn ideas into impact, powered by AI and driven by human ingenuity.

Adobe's Marketing Finance organization is reinventing how it operates from the ground up, with workflow automation and AI at the center. This role makes that happen. About the Role
The Global Microsoft GTM Lead owns the strategic partnership between Adobe and Microsoft. You will set and execute the joint go-to-market strategy, expand customer relationships and Azure Marketplace adoption, and align executives, field teams, product, and marketing across both companies. As the primary liaison between Adobe and Microsoft, you are accountable for revenue growth, cloud adoption, seller enablement, and delivery of the joint business plan.

The partner ecosystem is early, programs are still being designed, and you will work across three organizations (including SIs) whose incentives on any given deal don’t always align. You will help shape how frontier AI technology reaches the enterprise through the services ecosystem.

Strategy and Execution
Own the end-to-end GTM strategy and operation of the alliance, prioritizing high-value enterprise opportunities and driving revenue through Microsoft field engagement and joint co-sell motions.
Decide where to concentrate investment across the partner portfolio, and make the case to stop investing where returns are not there.
Provide market intelligence and competitive insight on the partner ecosystem to inform product and commercial strategy.
Partner with Adobe’s alliances, sales, partner marketing, and regional cloud teams to keep the motion consistent globally while regions execute locally.

Align executives, product teams, the Adobe-Microsoft partner team, sales leadership, and marketing around year-over-year revenue growth.
Coordinate stakeholders across sales, marketing, product, engineering, finance, and operations to drive accountability on strategic initiatives.

Represent customer and Microsoft requirements in product planning, using adoption metrics and usage telemetry to measure impact and business value.

Communication: Exceptional communication skills and executive presence, with the ability to influence senior internal and external stakeholders.

Airbnb is a creative company on a mission to connect people to the magic of the real world. As a Creative Lead (Art), you will be the visual driving force behind high-impact integrated campaigns and social work across our highest-growth verticals, including Home/Stay, Experiences, Services, and more.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Tech Foundations
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:
Airbnb's mission is to create a world where people can Belong Anywhere. Our community of guests and hosts rely on Airbnb around the clock to facilitate millions of stays and experiences per day.
The Observability team builds the platform Airbnb engineers use to understand how their systems behave in production. We collect, process, store, and query metrics, logs, events, and traces from both backend services and client apps. Our metrics platform alone ingests tens of millions of samples per second across more than a billion active time series. AI agents are now consumers of this data alongside engineers: they query telemetry to write and validate code and to help debug production issues. We continue to invest in reliable and efficient real time system for both AI and human access.

Building a fast, reliable query layer for both engineers and AI agents, with rate limiting, access control, isolation, and caching so agent traffic does not slow down incident response.
Giving teams self-service visibility and control over their telemetry cost: unit cost per team and service, and controls for granularity, sampling, and retention.
Improving time to detect with anomaly detection and automated correlation across signals.

You will act as the key partner between ABM stakeholders, cross-functional teams (Martech teams, Marketing Operations, and our Integrated Demand Center), and external vendors, translating strategic ABM objectives into scalable solutions.
This role combines strategic thinking with a builder mindset. You will not simply route requirements to a cross-functional support team — you will assess ABM requirements, and where a solution can be built using out-of-the-box AI tools (such as Amazon Quick, MCP integrations, and Asana), you will build it and enable ABMers to use these solutions effectively. Key job responsibilities
• Serve as the business lead for ABM AI, data, and operational solutions end-to-end — define the vision, program strategy, requirements, and success criteria for AI-based ABM solutions with limited guidance, operating in problem spaces where the solution is not yet defined.
• Design and build AI-powered tools and automation flows from problem definition through production — including customer journey engines, Quick Skill automations, MCP integrations across enterprise platforms (CRM, Highspot, Asana), and reactive signal-monitoring layers that keep solutions current as accounts evolve.
• Drive delivery and support of complex, cross-functional solutions — including design, AppSec compliance, build, user acceptance testing with field practitioners, documentation (SOPs and training guides), product demonstrations, and global rollout.
• Serve as the key partner between marketing stakeholders, cross-functional teams (Martech teams, Marketing Operations, and our Integrated Demand Center), and external vendors — translating business requirements into technical specifications, and communicating technical constraints back to marketing stakeholders.
• Drive AI enablement and adoption across a globally distributed practitioner community — assess AI maturity, build leveling frameworks, deploy Quick Skills tooling, and coach practitioners (e.g., via a Champions program) to scale adoption across all Geos.
• Spot risks and drive appropriate trade-offs — understand design approaches within the ABM technology domain (AI/ML frameworks, MCP integrations, data sources, agent orchestration, UI/UX) and ask the right questions to ensure sound decisions.
• Define, track, and report on program KPIs (adoption, usage volume, practitioner impact, time savings, delivery quality). Use data to identify bottlenecks, drive improvements, and inform investment decisions.
• Create new processes and mechanisms — AI solution generation workflows, orchestration patterns, coaching methodologies, and global rollout mechanisms — and optimize cross-team delivery across engineering and marketing organizations.

- Experience using data and metrics to drive improvements

title: Principal Product Manager - Technical, AWS Proactive Security / Support Authorization, AWS Proactive Security - AWS Piezo
description:
The Mission
AWS customers trust us with their sensitive data. We are building AWS Support Authorization, the mechanism that puts the decision about Support access in the customer's hands. The customer defines what AWS personnel may do, scoped to their own resources and bound to their open support case, and sees the resulting access in CloudTrail. We are looking for a Principal Product Manager - Technical to own that product and define the experience every AWS service presents when it needs a customer's permission. Your work will change how AWS asks for access to customer content across its services, and it will carry to customer data protection at industry scale.
What You'll Own
You own the approval product end to end, from the API and console surfaces to the evidence a customer keeps afterward and the requirements AWS service teams build to. You define the approval model and the experience a customer moves through when AWS asks for permission, you set the success metrics, and you read the usage data to learn whether customers trust the control enough to use it. You partner with AWS Support, service teams, and Legal on what approval means in each operational context, and with GTM, Marketing, and PR on the strategy, messaging, and themes AWS uses to talk about customer approval and operator access, so what a customer hears matches what they find in the product.
The Product Challenge
A customer with an open case wants two things at once. They want to decide who touches their data, and they want their problem fixed now. Approval that feels meaningful to give takes effort to give, and the person paying that effort is already waiting on help. Designing an experience a customer trusts, can get through without stalling their own case, and recognizes whichever AWS service they called about is the center of this role. There is no predetermined answer. You define it, and you take the definition to the service teams that build to it.
The Impact
Your work will have CISO-level visibility. You write the decision narratives and investment proposals that set product direction, and you take them to VPs and the CISO. You set requirements for engineering teams that do not report to you, and you earn adoption by being right and being clear. You represent the product directly to customers in financial services, healthcare, and the public sector, who ask hard questions about who at a provider can reach their data. As the capability reaches the rest of AWS, the experience you define becomes the way AWS asks for a customer's permission.
What We're Looking For
You are a product manager with real technical depth and a long view. You think about what this product should be two and three years out, before customers have put words to the requirement, and about what it says about AWS to a customer deciding where to run a regulated workload. You have defined a platform product that other engineering teams adopted and built on without reporting to you, and you did it by writing requirements clear enough to survive contact with engineering. You read an authorization or access-control architecture closely enough to know which models a given service can implement. You work across the whole AWS portfolio, where services differ in how they are built and operated, and you guide VPs and directors on where the product goes next. You hold opinions about security and permissions experiences and you back them with customer evidence. You set strategy while the customer requirements are still being discovered, and you own the call when security and customer convenience pull against each other. You have worked with product marketing and PR on positioning a capability whose value is trust, and you have sat across from a regulated customer and answered hard questions about provider access. You develop other product managers as the product grows past what one person owns.
Key job responsibilities
Own the customer experience for AWS Support Authorization end to end: how a customer learns Support needs access, what the request tells them, how they decide, what proof they keep afterward. Define the consent model, covering approval granularity, defaults, duration, revocation behavior mid-case, and the evidence a customer receives. Set the requirements AWS services build to as the capability reaches the rest of AWS, and decide which elements a service team may shape to its own workflow. Own the API and console product surfaces. Define the success metrics and read the usage data to learn how customers respond to consent requests. Partner with AWS Support and service teams on what consent means in each operational context, and bring in Legal on the commitments the product makes to customers. Partner with GTM, Marketing, and PR on how AWS positions customer consent and operator access. Write the decision narratives and investment proposals that set product direction and present them to VP and CISO-level leadership. Represent the product directly to customers. Mentor PMTs and contribute to PMT assessments.
A day in the life
The AWS Proactive Security team builds the controls that protect customer data at scale. You start the day in the usage data, looking at how customers responded to consent requests over the past week and what that says about the experience. You meet a service team preparing to adopt Support Authorization, work through how consent should present for their access patterns, and decide what their integration can and cannot vary. Midday you review messaging with Marketing so the way AWS describes customer consent matches what the console does. In the afternoon you write: a narrative on where the consent model goes over the next two years, for a review with VPs and the CISO. You close the day on a call with a regulated customer walking them through the control and hearing what still gives them pause.

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.
