description:
Data Center Serviceability team works with hundreds of data centers globally to deliver the highest quality and lowest cost availability, capacity, and scaling results for our customers. We standardize operations globally by delivering tools, policy, processes, and procedures to our internal teams.
Serviceability is the ability to maintain, repair, and manage infrastructure assets efficiently throughout their lifecycle, encompassing maintenance standards, spares management, training and certifications, operational readiness, and the systematic use of data and automation to prevent disruptions and drive continuous improvement.
We are seeking a Technical Program Manager to support serviceability for water systems across our data centers. Water quality management is a critical and fast-growing area of data center operations, where evaporative cooling, condenser water, and makeup water systems must be kept safe, compliant, and reliable to protect both people and infrastructure. This role will define how water systems are sampled, maintained, and kept within regulatory compliance as we scale from early programs to a global fleet, with a focus on proactively catching water quality issues before they drive equipment degradation or infrastructure downtime.
What you will do:
You will own the serviceability program for water systems across the fleet. You will write and maintain preventive maintenance (PM) guidelines for water sampling across all water bodies in our data centers, such as cooling towers, condenser and chilled water loops, evaporative systems, and storage tanks, making sure these guidelines meet regulatory and environmental compliance requirements across every region we operate in. You will build these guidelines with Operations, Data Center Engineering Operations (DCEO), Industrial Hygiene, Environmental, and water treatment vendors. You will set the serviceability framework for water systems so that sampling, treatment, and remediation happen on time and water quality issues are caught proactively rather than after they affect equipment or availability. You will partner with Finance on labor analyses that turn sampling and treatment needs into staffing plans. You will work with Field Engineering to lead root cause analyses on water quality and equipment findings, and you will make sure the lessons feed back into PM standards and procedures. You will work with Operations and site teams to build operational readiness plans for new sites, then track readiness so every site is sampling and compliant from day one. You will also run field trials and stakeholder workshops to validate procedures, collect feedback and drive continuous improvement.
Key job responsibilities
Own the execution and success metrics for water systems serviceability across the global fleet
Write and maintain PM guidelines for water sampling across all water bodies, ensuring they meet regulatory and environmental compliance, working with Operations, DCEO, Industrial Hygiene, Environmental, and vendors
Set the serviceability framework for water systems that keeps sampling and treatment on schedule and prevents water quality issues from causing infrastructure downtime
Build mechanisms to proactively detect and escalate water quality risks before they affect equipment or availability
Conduct labor analyses with Finance to support annual and long-range staffing plans
Lead root cause analyses with Field Engineering on water quality and equipment findings, and drive corrective actions into standards
Build operational readiness plans with Operations and site teams, and track readiness as new sites deploy
Run field trials and stakeholder workshops to validate procedures and collect operational feedback
Keep serviceability standards current as the fleet grows and new equipment, regulations, and vendors are introduced
Use data and metrics to measure program health, prioritize effort and report progress
Write narratives (one to six pages) and present to Director-level leadership
Travel up to 10–15%

description:

Willingness to travel domestically and internationally.

Acoustic and vibration measurement skills with experience making measurements in anechoic/hemi-anechoic chambers and with data analysis /signal processing methodologies.

title: Camera Algorithms Engineer

title: Engineering Manager, Bazel & Remote Build Execution

title: Materials Scientist - Capacitors
description:
Join Apple's innovative hardware team as a Materials Scientist for Capacitors, where you will own Apple's technology strategy across the polymer, electrolytic, film, and safety capacitor families — driving critical component solutions from initial concept to high-volume mass production across all Apple product lines.
In this senior role, you will serve as the primary technical expert bridging Apple's cross-functional teams with our global network of capacitor suppliers across the full non-MLCC capacitor space: tantalum polymer (including PFAS-free transition), aluminum polymer, aluminum electrolytic, film, safety/Y-rated, and emerging electrochemical energy storage technologies. You will be responsible for predicting component performance from supplier process choices — pellet morphology and sintering chemistry, oxide film formation kinetics, foil etch architecture, winding geometry, and conductive polymer chemistry — rather than relying on datasheet specifications, and will set Apple's technology direction across these families 3+ years ahead of integration. You will work closely with our existing Passive Component Technologists, SI/PI teams, LOB EEs, and commodity managers across iPhone, iPad, Watch, Mac, AirPods, Vision, Power Adapters, and beyond. This is an exceptional opportunity for a scientist or engineer with deep materials science or electrochemistry expertise who is passionate about making a significant impact at Apple. This role requires approximately 10–20% overseas travel.
Minimum qualifications: Deep Polymer, Film, and Safety Capacitor Expertise — Extensive professional experience across tantalum polymer (MnO₂ and conductive-polymer types, including PFAS-free pellet and termination chemistry), aluminum polymer & electrolytic (etch architecture, conductive layer deposition, ESR/ESL behavior), film capacitor construction (winding geometry, self-healing metallization, voltage derating), and safety/Y-rated capacitors (safe-failure construction, IEC 60384-14 X/Y classification, creepage and clearance). Proficiency in material characterization, DC-bias degradation, surge and leakage current reliability, and construction-to-performance modeling is required.
Materials Science and Electrochemistry Depth — Command of the physical mechanisms driving capacitor behavior: dielectric oxide formation kinetics (Ta₂O₅, Al₂O₃), pellet porosity and sintering, polymer conductivity and thermal stability, self-healing metallization failure modes, leakage current mechanisms, and capacitor-level safe-failure design. Ability to challenge and evaluate supplier process and material claims from first principles.
Cross-Disciplinary Knowledge — Familiarity with PDN and EMI filter circuit topologies, power supply design, IEC safety standards and regulatory frameworks (including PFAS/REACH restrictions and their supply-chain implications), and device-level reliability requirements across consumer electronics product categories.
Program Management and Influence — Proven ability to work as an individual contributor within a highly cross-functional environment. Must possess strong interpersonal skills to identify technical challenges, engage with suppliers, drive solutions, and manage development programs to successful and on-schedule delivery.
Hands-On Manufacturing Experience — A minimum of 5 years (preferably in a recent role) of direct, on-site factory floor experience with capacitor manufacturing processes is mandatory.
Education and Experience — PhD in Materials Science & Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Chemistry, or Physics with a minimum of 5 years of relevant professional experience in capacitor or passive component technologies.
Preferred qualifications: Solid track record of leading passive component product development from concept to mass-production across multiple capacitor technology families
Experience with PFAS-free materials qualification and supplier transition management
Familiarity with MLCC ceramic dielectric R&D and supercapacitor / EDLC construction and reliability limits is a plus
In-depth knowledge of capacitor supply chains, including tantalum ore sourcing, aluminum foil markets, and polymer electrolyte supply base
Strong interpersonal skills and demonstrated cross-LOB technical collaboration

title: Network Business Development & Partnership Manager  - Wallet, Payments, and Commerce
description:

title: PMU Design Verification Engineer: Analog & Mixed Signal Engineer
description:

In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring high quality silicon for IC chips and IPs. Daily work involves verification of mixed signal IC designs using a combination of analog circuits and RTL in the same simulation. Responsibilities include all phases of pre-silicon verification from early discussions with architects, reviewing specifications, writing verification plans, running simulations, triaging issues, and reviewing results with the team.
• Develop detailed test and coverage plans based on IC specifications.
• Completion of verification plans from beginning to end: test bench and environment bring-up, regressions, failure debug, and tape-out.
• Develop verification methodology suitable for the IP, ensuring scalability and portability.
• Develop verification environment, including stimuli, checkers, assertions, trackers, and coverage.
• Sign-off mixed signal designs in preparation for tapeout.

Proficient in hardware descriptive languages: Verilog, System-Verilog, and/or Verilog-AMS code.
Familiarity with authoring analog assertion checks to catch bugs.
Capability to identify failure mechanisms and review verification results in analog IC designs.
Ability to write test plans, present results, and communicate clearly with multi-functional teams.
Comfortable with running simulations through compute clusters while optimizing simulation and wall time.
Understanding of both power management and related auxiliary circuitry: switching converters, linear converters, reference circuitry, bandgaps, data converters, and/or clock generators.
Have a familiarity with verification methodologies and tools: simulators, waveform viewers, execution automation, coverage collection, gate level simulations.
Experience developing scalable and portable test benches.
A background that includes scripting or programming languages is preferred. These include, but are not limited to, TCL, Skill, Python, and/or PERL.
Your familiarity with analog behavioral models is also a plus.

title: Technical Content Engineer, Claris
description:

We're looking for a Technical Content Engineer who brings the practical skills of a software developer to our documentation team, and who will grow into the judgment of an excellent technical writer with support from our editorial team. You'll build and maintain the tools, pipelines, and workflows that make our documentation team faster and more accurate — and you'll author customer-facing content directly as you develop that expertise. This role combines hands-on engineering and automation with technical writing, docs-as-code practices, and thoughtful use of AI.
You'll work within Documentation & Localization and partner closely with engineering, product, and our team of experienced technical writers. The engineering work is central to this role: you'll design, build, test, and maintain the software systems — CI/CD pipelines, validation tooling, AI-assisted workflows, and integrations — that let our documentation keep pace with a fast-changing product. Alongside that, you'll author and maintain customer-facing documentation in assigned areas as you build your technical-writing craft.
The role is designed around an intended long-term balance of approximately 50% engineering and 50% technical content, reviewed across a quarter rather than enforced week to week. In your first year, expect the split to lean more heavily toward engineering while you build out core systems and ramp up on writing craft in parallel.

Experience with Git-based collaborative development, code review, and implementing or debugging CI/CD workflows.
Ability to write automated tests, diagnose failures, and explain the maintenance tradeoffs of your own code.
Practical experience integrating AI/LLM-based tools into a repeatable workflow, with a way of evaluating output quality and handling failure.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, and genuine interest in developing technical-writing craft with team mentorship.
Ability to investigate unfamiliar technical behavior, collaborate effectively with engineers and writers, and independently deliver a well-scoped project.
Preferred qualifications: Experience with docs-as-code environments, static site generators, or CCMS/help-authoring tools.
Experience with API documentation, schema-driven reference generation, or automated example/code testing.
Experience building or maintaining a search/retrieval system, embeddings pipeline, or MCP-style integration.
Prior technical-writing experience or coursework, even if not professional.
Familiarity with FileMaker.

title: Technology and Metrology Engineering Program Manager - Sensors
description:
Apple is where you go to do your life’s best work. Apple crafts consumer electronics that have touched millions and changed the way people harmonize with electronic devices around the world. HWTE is responsible for designing and developing methodologies and measurement solutions for calibration and validation of key technologies across Apple’s products. For new technologies, we focus on metrology development and design characterization. The team takes on a multitude of imaging & sensing technologies across all product lines. We are looking for an expert, technical leader with experience in touch sensing hardware to join the team championing calibration and test strategy through engagement in early stages of technology development. If you have broad experience across key hardware technologies, a strong product/customer focus, experience guiding sophisticated programs through the development process, and the ability to distill tradeoffs down to key factors and drive critical technology and product decisions we’d love to hear from you.
The Technology Program Office in Hardware Test Engineering (HWTE) champions technology calibration and test strategy while balancing between quality/customer experience with operational requirements. In this highly cross functional role, we are looking for leaders to engage in early stages of technology development supporting prototyping, design validation, simulation & metrology development activities, as well as identifying mass production intent solutions. 5+ years relevant industry experience in sensing technologies

10+ years relevant industry experience in sensing technologies
Background in touch design and touch-sensing technologies
Understanding of hardware/software architecture and interoperability of complex systems

title: Video Processing Engineer
description:
Do you love problem solving in a collaborative environment and then having the results of your efforts benefitting millions around the world? At Apple, our Architecture group is responsible for connecting our hardware and software into one unified system. Join this team, and you’ll collaborate with engineers across Apple to design how all of our technologies work in unison! You’ll drive development of our renowned system-on-a-chip architecture and develop algorithms to improve image quality and enable new use cases. You’ll develop forward-looking prototype systems as well as build and deploy software development tools that will be distributed to the Apple engineering community and help build the seamless technology experiences we’re known for worldwide.
This role will be responsible for investigating techniques for improving video processing solutions along the quality vs. power axes. State-of-the-art video processing solutions often involve the use of Machine Learning, but this can be computationally intensive and not practical. There exists a computational gap between Machine Learning techniques and traditional methods. The goal is to find operating points in between that can leverage the improved quality due to Machine Learning when needed and fall back to traditional, low-compute methods when not needed. Examples of video processing solutions that can benefit from using a hybrid solution comprised of traditional techniques and Machine Learning based techniques include (but not limited to) 1) Under Display Camera enhancement 2) Motion Estimation for Codec, GGM and MCTF 3) Face ID processing. The result of finding hybrid solutions is better video quality and/or longer battery life on the Phone, Pad and Mac. You will be responsible for investigating hybrid video processing techniques that can be translated into efficient SoC architectures. You will be expected to be able to translate architectures into specifications and C-models. You will also be expected to work cross-functionally with other Architects as well as Design and DV.
• Investigate and develop hybrid video processing architectures.
• Support chip architecture team and software teams to map algorithms into well-defined architectures that can be implemented in software and/or hardware.
• Generate architecture test vectors for quality validation.
• Write bit exact C-models of defined architectures.
• Support Design and Verification teams when verifying designs against bit exact C-models.
Minimum qualifications: BS degree
Ability to program in the following languages: Python, PyTorch and/or C/C++
Understanding of image/video/signal processing fundamentals
Understanding of neural network fundamentals
Preferred qualifications: MS or PhD degree or 3+ years of experience
Demonstrated ability of developing new image/video processing algorithms
Experience in developing neural network based image/video processing algorithms
Communication skills and ability to work across various groups
Understanding of fixed point representation and processing and/or ability to write bit-accurate software models
Understanding of pipelining and pixel processing architectures
Knowledge of computer architecture fundamentals

title: WiFi MAC Design Verification Engineer
description:

The ideal candidate will excel in detailed test planning, adapt to evolving requirements, build test bench infrastructure, perform regressions, close coverage, and leverage various AI tools to streamline DV processes and expedite debugging. If you’re passionate about contributing to products that have a global impact and want to advance your technical expertise, we’d love to hear from you.

Knowledge of standard ASIC design and verification flows, simulation and testbench development.
Skills with constrained random testing, coverage closure, gate level simulations.

Advanced knowledge of System Verilog and the UVM methodology.

And you will do it all in a collaborative environment that values your insight, encourages you to take on new responsibility, promotes continuous learning, and rewards innovation.

You will work cross-functionally with partners responsible for digital product development, marketing, and fraud to identify the best intent to realize our vision and develop go-to-market strategies to help launch this intent. You will take a hypothesis-driven analytical approach to support setting strategy, building business cases, testing outcomes, and measuring impact.
General Responsibilities:
Strategic leadership: Develop business strategies that will drive growth, profitability, and competitive success for Capital One in the face of shifting consumer and regulatory demands
Leadership: May manage and develop 1-2 analysts. Coaching and mentoring associates with a goal of developing and retaining talent at Capital One
Product: Develop and implement new product and pricing strategies for various lending products; lead product level modeling/analytics
Marketing: Lead direct-to-consumer marketing efforts for select products, and strategic intent for products distributed through the retail channel. Build targeted insights to inform the design and development of new customer experiences, as well as breakthrough technology and concepts designed to deliver on new go-to-market strategies
Credit Risk: Drive step-change improvements in credit performance by connecting drivers of future consumer credit trends to historical behavior, creating risk models, and testing hypotheses using rigorous monitoring and analysis
Execution: Manage and sequence delivery of business intent, build business requirements and execute against the product strategy. Oversee multiple projects and programs concurrently
Partnership: Work closely with colleagues across Capital One including: IT, Sales, Operations, Finance and others to drive improvement in quality, volume, service, and profitability
Strategic & analytic orientation: A proven track record of decision making and problem solving based on analytics. You’ll team with world-class professionals to develop and test strategies that ultimately impact the bottom line. And you will do it all in a collaborative environment that values your insight, encourages you to take on new responsibility, promotes continuous learning, and rewards innovation.
You will help shape product development, quantify new opportunities, and identify upcoming challenges.  You will  help define the methodologies for how we measure success, serving as the subject matter expert in experimentation, causal inference, and metrics selection. Your work will help partner teams prioritize what to build, set goals, and understand their impact.
Your work will directly influence product direction, investment decisions, and the product vision for the Retail Bank. You will help drive product led growth by employing a varied toolkit of rigorous analytical approaches, different statistical methodologies, and frameworks to surface insights on new and exciting opportunities and challenges. This is a highly collaborative role in which you will problem solve alongside partners and leadership in Product, Engineering, Research, Data, Finance, and others.

Product Strategy & Roadmap Influence: Partner closely with Product Management and Engineering to identify high-leverage growth opportunities. Translate complex behavioral data and user funnels into actionable product recommendations and feature requirements.
Experimentation & Causal Inference: Serve as internal authority on experimentation and causal inference. Define and enforce the standards for randomization, power analysis, and conversion window modeling. Design, analyze, and interpret complex A/B/n tests using advanced statistical techniques (randomization, power calculations, variance reduction, quasi-experiments) to isolate true customer incrementality.
Hands-On Technical Execution: Query, clean, and transform massive, complex datasets using SQL, Python, or R. Develop statistical models, user segmentation frameworks, and exploratory analysis to uncover engagement patterns.
Cross-Functional Leadership & Alignment: Drive alignment across cross-functional partners (Product, Tech, Research, Finance). Facilitate peer review gates to maintain rigorous analytical integrity and establish standardized KPI frameworks.
Data Storytelling & Executive Communication: Synthesize multi-faceted data insights into clear, strategic narratives. Able to influence audiences beyond vanity metrics to focus on underlying customer value and long-term business impact.

Proven Track Record: A seasoned analytical expert with significant experience in high-velocity product environments (e.g., e-commerce, fin-tech, or SaaS). You have navigated complex, ambiguous zero-to-one challenges and delivered clear outcomes.
Technical Mastery: Fluency in SQL and Python is a baseline requirement. Deep expertise in statistical modeling, DoE (Design of Experiments), and causal inference methodologies is critical.
Influencer Mindset: You possess strong executive communication skills and the ability to drive agreement through intellect and interpersonal negotiation rather than hierarchy. You can explain the "why" behind a complex statistical result to non-technical partners.
Product Sense: You understand how digital products are built, instrumented, and scaled. You know when to utilize centralized, self-serve experimentation tools versus when a high-bar, gate-kept methodology is required.

DoorDash’s DashOS business helps merchants grow and operate their businesses through technology that connects their own customer channels with the broader DoorDash ecosystem. Within DashOS, our business brings together hardware, software, payments, and ordering integrations to improve restaurant operations and merchant outcomes.
Our Strategy & Operations team turns merchant needs and business opportunities into product and go-to-market priorities, then builds the operating capabilities needed to deliver them. We work across Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Finance, and Revenue Operations to build and scale this business.
About the Role
We are looking for a Director of Strategy & Operations to set the strategic direction and lead business operations within DashOS. You will translate a long-term vision into financial plans, product and go-to-market priorities, and an operating model that supports growth, merchant retention, and healthy unit economics.
You will lead the Strategy & Operations team, with direct ownership of product operations, and partner closely with leaders across go-to-market, launch and implementation, support, and account management. You will help design the operating model across these functions and stay closely involved in the merchant experience as the business scales. As a leader of managers and operators, you will build the team and systems needed to grow, align cross-functional leaders around shared outcomes, and navigate decisions involving merchant needs, growth, profitability, and partner dependencies. This role requires an entrepreneurial leader who can identify new opportunities, make thoughtful decisions amid uncertainty, and stay close to the operational details that drive results.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Set the strategy and own business performance. Define the long-term direction, target merchant segments, and differentiation for our DashOS business. Lead annual and quarterly planning, developing financial forecasts and resourcing plans in partnership with Finance to align business needs with broader budget parameters and targets. Translate those plans into priorities that drive growth, retention, and healthy unit economics.
Shape the product and growth roadmap. Partner with Product and Engineering to translate merchant needs, market insights, and operational data into priorities across hardware, software, payments, and integrations. Identify and validate new use cases, product opportunities, and commercial approaches, including expansion into full-service restaurants.
Lead go-to-market strategy. Partner with Sales, Marketing, and Revenue Operations on positioning, merchant targeting, sales effectiveness, pricing, deal governance, and incentives that accelerate adoption and support sustainable growth.
Design and scale the operating model. Own product operations and partner with post-sales leaders to design the processes, handoffs, and systems supporting merchant launch, adoption, support, and retention. Stay close to execution and merchant feedback to identify gaps and drive improvements as the business scales, using experimentation, automation, and AI to improve how teams work.
Align leaders and navigate strategic tradeoffs. Build cross-functional alignment around shared goals and communicate clear recommendations to executives on strategy, performance, and investment needs. Guide decisions on critical partnerships and integrations, balancing merchant experience, growth, profitability, and business risk .
Develop a strong leadership team. Hire and coach managers and operators, strengthen leadership depth and succession, and establish clear accountability. Create an environment where teams collaborate effectively, challenge assumptions, and deliver sustainable results.
We’re excited about you because…
You have 12+ years of  experience leading strategy and operations in a complex, high-growth business, with a track record of building new offerings and scaling them into sustainable businesses.
You have 7+ years of experience leading multidisciplinary organizations through managers and built strong teams through thoughtful organization design, hiring, coaching, and leadership development.
You combine strategic thinking, analytical judgment, and product sense with a strong understanding of financial planning, pricing, and unit economics.
You understand how go-to-market execution and post-sales operations work together to drive adoption, retention, and profitable growth, and have partnered across these functions to build effective operating models. Experience in restaurant technology, POS, payments, or B2B SaaS is a plus.
You communicate clearly with executives, build trust across functions, and influence decisions and outcomes beyond your direct team.
You solve problems from first principles and move comfortably between long-term strategy and operational detail. You thrive in ambiguity, test assumptions, and use AI and automation to improve how your team works.

We're looking for someone to help scale DoorDash's next billion dollar business, DashMart, by growing our in-house food program, DashMart Kitchens. The DashMart Kitchens team is focused on building a new type of restaurant platform within DashMart, offering a broad selection of prepared foods and well-known restaurant staples to our customers' doorsteps.
About the Role
As the Kitchen Manager for DashMart Kitchens (DMK), you’ll lead the daily operations of a DoorDash-owned kitchen located within a DashMart fulfillment center. You’ll oversee a team of operations associates and shift leads to ensure every meal is prepared safely, efficiently, and to the highest quality standards.
You’ll combine hands-on culinary leadership with operational excellence — managing staffing, scheduling, and kitchen performance while ensuring food safety, order accuracy, and team success. You’ll work closely with your Site Manager to lead multiple food concepts, improve processes, and create a great place to work. In addition to leading the kitchen, you'll be cross trained into DashMart operations and expected to work on both sides of the business. This role requires strict adherence to food safety, inventory controls, and safety protocols due to routine access to food, supplies, equipment, and operational systems.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you...
Enjoy learning how different parts of a complex operation connect and are excited to collaborate cross-functionally
Are passionate about food and love to lead across multiple food concepts
Enjoy building processes and seeing ideas come to life
Are passionate about creating food consistently
Want to grow in delivery-only kitchen operations
Thrive in hands-on, fast-paced leadership roles.

You’ll hire, coach and develop high-performing team members, while building a safety-first culture where employees are excited to drive success, personally and for the team. You will refine processes, and partner with your Site Manager and cross-functional teams to execute new initiatives and continuously improve how the kitchen operates.

You will coach your team to maintain recipe accuracy, food safety, and storefront availability, knowing that consistency is key in a multi-concept kitchen. You have 3+ years of experience in a medium/high-volume fast-casual or full-service restaurant environment.
You have 1+ years of experience leading teams, including hiring, scheduling, coaching, and performance management.

title: Manager, Lease Accounting
description:
About the Team
The DoorDash Lease Accounting team ensures DoorDash’s lease portfolio is reported accurately and on time under ASC 842. This requires deep technical accounting review and careful interpretation of complex, often ambiguous lease arrangements. As the portfolio grows in size and complexity, we continue to strengthen our processes to keep pace with the business.
About the Role
You will report to the Senior Accounting Manager on our Lease Accounting team. As the Lease Accounting Manager, you will be a key technical expert on ASC 842, ensuring DoorDash’s leases are accounted for accurately as the business grows. This role is built for someone who takes ownership, stays ahead of the work, and works closely with partners across functions. Success means well-supported conclusions and dependable reporting each period, with the opportunity to apply your expertise to increasingly complex leases.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Review lease abstractions against new lease agreements and lease modifications to ensure accurate classification and recognition of each lease in accordance with ASC 842.
Perform detailed accounting analysis of complex lease arrangements and unique scenarios that go beyond standard treatment, documenting conclusions and supporting analysis.
Perform lease monthly close activities including journal entries, account reconciliations, and flux analysis
Own lease financial reporting deliverables, including cash flows, rollforwards, and disclosures.
Partner closely with Real Estate, Lease Administration and other cross-functional teams to understand lease activity early and keep the accounting accurate and timely.
Proactively identify and lead process improvements and automation initiatives to reduce manual work and improve the accuracy and efficiency of processes.
Maintain lease SOX controls and support both internal and external audit requests.
We’re excited about you because…
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, or a related field, and/or equivalent work experience.
6+ years accounting experience, including in-depth experience applying US GAAP lease accounting (ASC 842), which is essential to this role.
Proven experience reviewing lease agreements, interpreting lease terms, and assessing their financial implications to determine the appropriate accounting treatment.
Ownership mindset and proactiveness, with a track record of managing multiple deliverables and following them through to completion on close timelines.
Strong cross-functional partnership and communication skills to work effectively with internal and external partners.
Close attention to detail and demonstrated problem-solving skills.

DoorDash is seeking a Staff Manufacturing Test Engineer to lead production testing for Dot, our autonomous road-going delivery robot. description:
About the Team
DoorDash Labs is an independent team within DoorDash. We explore robotics and automation to transform last mile logistics in the long term. If you have a passion for applying robotics solutions in a service used by millions of people, then we want to talk to you!
About the Role
We're hiring a State Estimation & Perception Engineer in our Autonomy Software team. In this role, you'll own and develop the perception and state estimation for our package pickup and delivery system. You'll influence system design decisions, including sensor selection, sensing architecture, and observability analysis, at the earliest stage when choices still matter.
You're excited about this opportunity because you will…
Play an integral role on a small and focused team
Own tuning and implementation of the state estimation stack on the drone (PX4 EKF modifications, fault tolerance, multi-sensor fusion with VIO and laser odometry)
Own state estimation and perception of the delivery mechanism, including dynamics modeling, observation model design, and sensor selection
Work closely with controls and planning to close the loop on automated pickup and delivery
Work closely with the hardware team to define sensing principles and sensor placement
Design and execute flight test campaigns to validate estimator performance
Identify and resolve failure modes in estimation (degenerate geometries, sensor dropout, initialization)
We're excited about you because…
You have deep experience with state estimation and filtering (EKF, UKF, MSCKF, particle filters)
You have experience with optimization-based methods (factor graphs, GTSAM, Ceres, SymForce)
You have experience with visual-inertial odometry (VIO) and/or laser odometry (LIO)
You're proficient in modern computer vision (feature extraction, tracking, depth estimation)
You have strong C++ and/or Rust skills, with Python for prototyping and analysis
You have experience deploying estimation on real hardware with real sensor noise
You can derive an EKF from scratch, including process model, measurement model, observability analysis, and consistency checks
You have deep linear algebra knowledge (matrix decompositions, sparsity exploitation, numerical conditioning)
You've closed a perception-to-control loop on real hardware under degraded conditions
You're comfortable operating at the intersection of theory and embedded reality
You're driven by a passion for delivering outstanding customer experiences
You have a proactive approach to development, often crafting new tools
MS/PhD degree in CS, EE, ME, Robotics, or related technical field
Nice to have experience includes
Experience with PX4 / ArduPilot EKF internals
Experience with multi-body state estimation (tethered or suspended payloads)
Familiarity with SLAM in GPS-denied environments
Publications or open-source contributions in state estimation or VIO
You've debugged estimator failures in the field, not just in simulation

location: Seattle, WA; New York, NY; San Francisco, CA; Los Angeles, CA
description:
About the Team
DoorDash for Business is building the premier corporate dining and benefits platform—helping companies of all sizes feed their teams through industry-leading products and meal programs. Our mission is to become the go-to solution for executives, administrators, and employees who need seamless, high-quality food programs at work. We move fast, operate with an ownership mindset, and are growing new product lines to better serve our corporate customers.
About the Role
As a Senior Associate on the DoorDash for Business Strategy & Operations team, you will help grow and run Self-Serve Meal Manager, our free, self-serve product that automates recurring meals for teams and offices. Because the product is self-serve, growth is product-led: customers find us, sign up, set up a calendar, and decide whether to stay without a sales rep in the loop. Your job is to make every stage of that funnel work better.
Acquire: Bring new teams in at the top of the funnel, both on the DoorDash platform (merchandising, in-app placements, lifecycle messaging) and off platform (paid, email, and organic channels).
Activate: Turn sign-ups into first orders through strong onboarding, and find and fix where customers drop off.
Retain: Keep teams ordering through a reliable, high-quality product experience, and catch the issues that cause churn before customers leave.
This is a role for someone versatile who will wear many hats: analyst, growth operator, customer-facing problem solver, and product partner. You will be expected to find a problem in the data, work out why it is happening, and drive the fix yourself. The role is built to grow. As the product scales, so will your scope and ownership.
You will report to the Manager, Strategy & Operations for DoorDash for Business and can work remotely or hybrid depending on preference.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Own the funnel: Analyze the self-serve funnel end to end, from visitor to sign-up to activation to repeat ordering. Find where customers drop off and run experiments on acquisition channels, onboarding, selection, and promotions to lift conversion and retention.
Go deep on the data: Write SQL daily to size problems, segment customers, measure lift, and tell a real result from noise. Build the dashboards and automated checks that let a small team support a growing customer base.
Work directly with customers: Email customers, resolve issues, and run proactive outreach to teams that are stuck, at risk, or churned. Hear first-hand why people stay and why they leave.
Turn issues into patterns: Translate individual customer problems into trends, then flag them to product and engineering with a clear call on severity: urgent and big, or real but minor, backed by the metric impact.
Improve reliability: Root cause order defects such as late deliveries, point of sale issues, and failed drop-offs. Work with merchants, Dashers, and support partners on fixes and track the impact on quality metrics.
Use AI to scale: Build AI-assisted workflows that flag at-risk customers, orders, and merchants, and replace slow manual analysis and one-off fixes with repeatable processes the team can maintain.
Influence the roadmap: Bring customer, merchant, and order data to product, engineering, and operations partners as clear recommendations.
We're excited about you because…
You have 2–5 years of experience in strategy and operations or growth, ideally at a marketplace company, a high-growth B2B startup, or an early-stage AI company.
You are deeply analytical. You write SQL fluently, are comfortable with large datasets, and can get to a root cause and turn complexity into a clear recommendation.
You have run growth or conversion experiments and can tell a real lift from noise.
You are hungry to learn and quick to pick up new domains, tools, and skills. You are versatile, happy to switch between analysis, customer conversations, and process building, and you want a role you can grow into.
You are comfortable in customer-facing work: writing clear emails, handling frustrated customers, and resolving issues with empathy and ownership.
You have a product mindset. You can spot patterns across customer issues and judge what is urgent and what is not, and you can make that case to product partners.
You are extremely comfortable using AI (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or similar) in your daily work to automate workflows, analyze data, and make faster, better decisions.
You own problems end to end, from diagnosis to testing to rollout, and are comfortable building processes in ambiguous, early-stage environments.
You communicate with clarity and influence, tailoring your message for customers, merchants, cross-functional partners, and senior leadership.

title: Executive Director, MISUMI Imprint Foundation
description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
About the Foundation
MISUMI Imprint Foundation is the first corporate giving organization in MISUMI Group 's history. It launched in October 2026 with a $2 million seed investment from MISUMI Americas and a mandate to fund the people who will build the physical world.
The reasoning is straightforward. MISUMI supplies the components that engineers design into machines, and as AI moves out of software and into factories, vehicles, operating rooms, and orbit, demand is rising for engineers, machinists, and technicians who can build hardware that works safely and reliably in the real world. The United States is not producing enough of them. The Foundation exists to widen that pipeline.
We make grants in three areas:
Scholarships & Access — need-based support for first-generation and underrepresented students in engineering, manufacturing, and supply chain, at four-year universities and community colleges alike
Maker Programs — equipment grants for manufacturing labs, engineering team sponsorships, maker spaces, and student hackathons
Industry–Academia Bridges — curricula built around real manufacturing problems, internship and apprenticeship pathways, mentorship and career support
The Foundation launched under the fiscal sponsorship of the SME Education Foundation and has filed for independent 501(c)(3) public charity status. Its defining structural feature is partner co-investment: MISUMI's global supplier partners are invited to contribute annually and join the Foundation Advisory Board, with seats at three tiers — Founding, Growth, and Community Partner.
About the role
This is a founding role. The mission is set, the seed capital is committed, and the board is in place. Almost everything else is yours to build: the first grant cycle, the review criteria, the partner program, the measurement framework, and the independent organization itself.
You will be the Foundation's first full-time employee and its public face — to universities and community colleges, to K–12 and robotics programs, to MISUMI's supplier partners, and to the press. You will report to the Board Chair and work closely with MISUMI Americas leadership, but the Foundation's day-to-day direction will be set by you.
We are looking for someone who wants the version of this job where the answers do not exist yet.
What you'll do
Build and run the grantmaking. Design the application, review, and award process across all three program areas. Source and evaluate grantees. Set award sizes and durations. Make the hard calls about what we fund and what we decline, and be able to explain both.
Grow the partner co-investment program. Recruit supplier partners into the Founding, Growth, and Community tiers. Run the Advisory Board, which convenes twice yearly to set grant priorities and announce awards jointly. Manage relationships with senior executives at some of the world's largest component manufacturers.

Account Executive, Flexport Capital
Flexport helps more than 10,000 clients and suppliers lead all aspects of their supply chain operations. Each of these customers faces significant working capital burdens that hamper their ability to grow their businesses. Since inception, Flexport Capital has provided over $2 billion in loans to Flexport customers to address these needs. Our non-dilutive capital products empower businesses to grow and bridge their working capital needs while maintaining ownership and control. As a start-up within a start-up, we’re developing unique fintech products that leverage the resources and data of Flexport’s platform for global trade. We are seeking an entrepreneurial and financially savvy individual to join our tight-knit team.

Own the full end-to-end sales cycle for your territory, from sourcing and prospecting through deal structuring, underwriting coordination, closing, and early relationship management.

Leverage Flexport's freight and omni capabilities to create working capital solutions that deepen customer relationships, increase wallet share, and win deals competitors can't.

Experience - 6+ years of experience in sales/sales development for a financial services and/or a technology company. Previous startup experience is a plus.
Financial & Credit Acumen - Fluency in working capital structures, financial statement analysis, and lending mechanics. You can read and interpret P&Ls, balance sheets, and cash flow statements to assess customer needs. You'll be expected to recommend appropriate lending structures and create tailored working capital solutions for each prospect based on their business model and financing needs.
Full-cycle sales execution - You’ve owned deals from prospect through close. You understand pipeline management, deal structuring, and how to navigate complex sales cycles. You’ve hit and exceeded quota consistently.

Commercial drive and ownership - You’re motivated by building and growing a business. You think like an owner, take accountability for outcomes, and proactively solve problems to move deals forward.
Strategic business sense - You see beyond individual deals. You understand market trends, competitive threats, and identify customer needs that create product/GTM opportunities.
Data & Tools - Proficiency in Salesforce, Excel, Claude, and other data tools. Ability to design dashboards and reporting frameworks to track pipeline growth and buying signals.

title: Associate Manager, Quality Engineering
description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

Form Energy is looking for a hands-on Associate Manager of Quality Engineering to lead a product quality engineering team on our factory floor. Reporting to the Quality Engineering Manager, you will operate with high autonomy to manage the day-to-day quality engineering activities across manufacturing lines — driving timely resolution of line issues, coaching a team of Quality Engineers, and ensuring our processes consistently meet specification. You will own the risk profile for your production lines, knowing where quality risk is concentrated and making fast, well-informed calls on how to manage it. You will work closely with Manufacturing Engineering, Production, and the broader Quality organization to keep the lines running at the quality level our products demand, while building the discipline and rigor of the team you lead. This is a role for someone who thrives in the detail of daily floor operations as much as in developing the people and processes that sustain quality at scale.

 Relocation assistance is available. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Lead and coach a team of Quality Engineers, setting daily priorities, developing their technical skills, and holding the team accountable to a high quality bar

 - Own the day-to-day execution of quality engineering activities across production lines, ensuring issues are triaged, escalated, and resolved quickly

 - Develop, maintain and continuously improve PFMEAs and Control Plans for your lines, keeping them aligned with current process risk and performance data

 - Lead execution of and training on mission-critical quality systems: Material Review Board (MRB), Process Change Requests (PCR), Production Part Approval Process (PPAP), Inspection Standards, Control Plans, SPC/Control Charts, Traceability, etc.

 - Manage the risk profile of production lines using quality metrics to identify where risk is concentrated, and drive continuous improvement in how that risk is mitigated over time

 - Own the creation and daily operation of Form Energy’s Quality Management Systems, ensuring regulatory compliance for safe development, production, and deployment of Form’s battery systems

 - Collaborate with cross-functional teams on continuous improvement activities, cost down initiatives, etc.

 - Facilitate, promote and train in the use of highly effective best practices




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - 3-5 years of experience in quality engineering or manufacturing, including experience leading or managing a technical team

 - Hands-on experience executing quality systems such as MRB, PCR, PPAP, Inspection Standards, Control Plans, SPC/Control Charts, and Traceability

 - Highly technical, with a strong foundation for logic that allows for a steep learning curve and the ability to adapt to new technologies.

 - Experience/expertise of various quality system methodologies including 8D (problem solving), SPC (data analytics), DOE (Design of Experiments), GD&T (Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing), RCA (root cause analysis), proper auditing techniques, design reviews, etc.

 - Excellent leadership, project management, communication, and organizational skills.

 - Bachelor’s Degree (or higher) in Engineering

You'll bring those capabilities together around a common goal: creating qualified pipeline and quantifying through data and insights what's driving it. As Formic grows, you'll help determine how the team and these capabilities evolve.
We're looking for someone who combines creativity with operating rigor. You'll set strategy, but you'll stay close enough to the work to understand what's actually happening. You'll establish clear priorities, ownership, and metrics, and make decisions based on results. When something works, you'll scale it. When it doesn't, you'll change it or stop doing it.
You'll also build and develop the team around you. That means setting clear expectations, delegating real ownership, coaching people to get better, and holding the team accountable for results. We want a leader who welcomes challenges, seeks out evidence that their assumptions may be wrong, and changes course when the data or the team tells them something different.
This is a builder role. One day you might be sharpening Formic's positioning; the next, reviewing pipeline performance with Sales, coaching an SDR, digging into why a campaign isn't converting, or working with a GTM Engineer to test a completely different way of reaching manufacturers. You should be equally comfortable asking "What should we try?" and "Did it work?"
We’re not looking for a standard B2B marketing playbook or activity for activity’s sake. We’re looking for a Head of Marketing who creates focus from ambiguity, turns experiments into learning, and builds repeatable systems that drive measurable business results.
You’ll bring a healthy appetite for the unconventional—challenging how things have always been done, proposing bold ideas, and testing them intelligently. We want the kind of imagination that makes people stop, pay attention, and think differently about industrial automation.
The next great idea in industrial marketing probably sounds a little crazy. Good. We want to hear it. Help us make industrial robotics impossible to ignore.
You will own the engine that feeds our sales and deployments.
In this role you will:
Own Brand & Marketing
Own Formic's marketing strategy and how we show up in the market.
Develop and continually sharpen our positioning, messaging, and story.
Translate Formic's technology, business model, and customer value proposition into messaging that resonates with manufacturers and their economic buyers.
Own content, creative, video, website, customer stories, events, campaigns, thought leadership, PR, product marketing, and other channels that build awareness and demand.
Develop differentiated messaging across industries, use cases, personas, and stages of the buying journey.
Demonstrated ability to conceive and execute original, unconventional marketing campaigns that break through industry norms, capture attention, and produce measurable business impact.
Turn customer outcomes, deployments, product capabilities, and what we're learning in the field into compelling content.
Build Formic's brand within manufacturing while ensuring our marketing investments support clear commercial objectives.
Own Demand & Pipeline Generation
Own the creation of qualified pipelines across Marketing, lead generation, SDR/outbound, ABM, events, paid, organic, partnerships, and emerging channels.
Establish clear pipeline goals and build repeatable systems to identify, engage, and qualify manufacturers that fit Formic's ideal customer profile, optimizing channel mix, conversion, and resources.
Lead and develop our Sales Development function, including targeting, prospecting strategy, messaging, sequencing, coaching, productivity, and performance.
Establish clear funnel definitions, ownership, lead routing, and follow-up processes to ensure every source of inbound and outbound interest is captured, acted upon, and effectively handed off to Sales.
Partner closely with Sales and RevOps on territory priorities, pipeline needs, lead quality, conversion, and feedback from the market.
Measure pipeline contribution, progression, conversion, and cost by source and channel, connecting marketing investments to closed-won revenue and informing where to invest, optimize, or stop.
Build Our GTM Innovation Capability
Lead our GTM Engineering capability, using AI, automation, data, enrichment, personalization, and emerging technologies to improve how we identify, reach, engage, and qualify potential customers.
Own the effectiveness and evolution of our marketing technology ecosystem, including CRM integrations, outbound platforms, lead routing, data quality, attribution, and reporting, in partnership with Sales and RevOps.
Build and optimize scalable systems for account identification, segmentation, prospecting, personalization, campaign execution, and lead management.
Evaluate existing tools and workflows, identifying opportunities to simplify, automate, integrate, consolidate, or eliminate work rather than defaulting to additional tools or headcount.
Drive disciplined experimentation across channels, technologies, data sources, and approaches, establishing clear hypotheses, measurable outcomes, and decisions about what to scale, change, or stop.
Ensure our GTM infrastructure is reliable, documented, and maintainable, with clear ownership, appropriate data governance, and minimal dependency on any single person or external partner.
Own the Funnel and the Numbers
Establish clear visibility into the entire funnel, from target account through qualified opportunity, pipeline progression, and revenue.
Define and own a focused set of metrics that measure pipeline creation, conversion, velocity, cost, channel effectiveness, and commercial impact.
Partner with Sales and RevOps to ensure reliable data, consistent reporting, and a shared understanding of performance.
Establish a disciplined operating cadence that translates performance insights into decisions about strategy, priorities, budget, and resources, holding the organization accountable for outcomes rather than activity.
Create Focus and Accountability
Translate broad company objectives into clear priorities, ownership, expectations, and measurable outcomes that connect the team's work to business goals.
Make disciplined decisions about priorities and resources, challenging assumptions, stopping initiatives that aren't delivering results, and adapting as we learn.
Stay close enough to the work to identify problems early, remove obstacles, and hold people accountable without becoming a bottleneck to execution.
Foster a culture of transparency, constructive challenge, and open communication about performance, priorities, tradeoffs, and lessons learned.
Establish accountability for external agencies, contractors, and technology partners, including deliverables, performance, costs, documentation, and continuity, while building sustainable processes that preserve institutional knowledge and support organizational change.
Build and Lead the Team
Lead and align af multidisciplinary organization spanning Marketing, content and creative, lead generation, Sales Development, and GTM Engineering around shared commercial goals.
Build a high-performing team by establishing clear expectations, delegating meaningful ownership, coaching and developing talent, and addressing performance gaps directly.
Assess existing capabilities, recognize and develop the strengths of the people already here, and determine what additional skills and resources we'll need as we grow.
Hire thoughtfully and build organizational capabilities that create leverage, rather than adding unnecessary layers or headcount.
Foster a culture of creativity, curiosity, accountability, experimentation, and continuous improvement, where people feel empowered to challenge assumptions and solve problems.
What Makes You a Great Fit:
Experience building and leading Marketing, Growth, Demand Generation, or similarly broad functions in high-growth B2B companies, with measurable commercial results.
A track record of building, improving, and scaling marketing and pipeline-generation systems, not simply inheriting and managing established operations.
Deep understanding of B2B demand generation, funnel economics, segmentation, conversion, attribution, and how Marketing, SDR, and Sales work together to create and convert pipeline.
Experience developing differentiated positioning and messaging for complex products, markets, and buying decisions.
Strong technical fluency and demonstrated experience evaluating, integrating, and optimizing marketing technology, data, automation, and AI-enabled GTM systems, with the ability to diagnose problems and make informed architectural decisions.
An AI-native mindset, with demonstrated ability to apply emerging technologies, experiment rigorously, evaluate results, and turn successful approaches into scalable capabilities.
Strong people leadership, including building and developing teams, delegating meaningful ownership, addressing performance gaps, and leading effectively through growth and organizational change.
An operating style that combines creativity, analytical rigor, intellectual flexibility, and accountability, with the judgment to challenge assumptions, make difficult tradeoffs, and change course when evidence warrants it.
The ability to operate strategically and tactically, creating clarity from ambiguity, communicating effectively across functions, and staying close enough to execution to understand and solve problems.
Bonus points if you have:
Experience in manufacturing, industrial automation, robotics, industrial technology, or similarly complex B2B markets with long sales cycles and multiple decision-makers.
Experience directly building or leading SDR organizations, including account-based and territory-based outbound strategies.
Experience building or leading GTM Engineering, Growth Engineering, or similar technical growth capabilities.
What Success Looks Like
Within your first year, Formic has a marketing and pipeline-generation engine that we understand, measure, and know how to scale.
We know who we should target, how to reach them, which messages resonate, which channels create qualified opportunities, what those opportunities cost, and where we should invest next.
There is clear ownership across the funnel. Marketing, lead generation, Sales Development, and GTM Engineering operate as one connected organization, with a tight feedback loop into Sales. The team knows what matters and what it's accountable for.
Experiments have hypotheses and measurable outcomes. Successful ideas become repeatable systems. Unsuccessful ones produce learning and stop consuming resources. Decisions about priorities, budget, and headcount are grounded in results.
Our marketing and GTM infrastructure is reliable, integrated, and well understood. We have confidence in our data, clear accountability for lead management, and systems that the team can operate and improve independently. Technology and vendor decisions are deliberate, economically justified, and aligned with our commercial priorities.
Most importantly, Sales has a consistent and growing flow of qualified opportunities, and we can explain what is creating them.
That's the engine you'll own.

Flexible Time Off: Take the time you need, when you need it, supported by our flexible PTO policy
Compensation Philosophy
Formic’s pay and equity packages are thoughtfully benchmarked against peer companies at a similar growth stage. Equity represents a meaningful part of our mutual investment: when Formic succeeds, so do you.
Final offers are customized based on experience, geographic location, market considerations, and a candidate’s preferred balance of cash and equity. Our goal is to attract and reward top talent who will have significant impact, and we are open to thoughtful discussions to align on the right structure.

We’re building this company from the ground up, and every person we hire has an outsized impact on our culture, performance, and trajectory. While each team member brings unique strengths and perspectives, we look for people who align with our Operating Principles and embody them in action. If this sounds like you, Formic may be the right place for you!
Fearless Optimism: You make bold bets and default optimistic. You believe in the mission, aren’t paralyzed by risk, and fear inaction more than failure. You see ambiguity as opportunity and bring energy to building what doesn’t yet exist.
Create the Magic: You absorb complexity so customers don’t have to. Whether your customer is external or internal, you focus on delivering experiences that are clear, fast, value-added, and outcome-driven. You don’t say “not my job.” You make things work.

The Finance Manager is the senior finance leader at the plant and the primary finance partner to the Plant Manager and operations leadership. Reporting to the Sr. Manager Finance, Operations, this role owns the financial performance of the plant. That includes building the annual budget and monthly forecasts, explaining results and variances, and turning operational data into actions that reduce cost and improve productivity.  The role leads daily, weekly and monthly performance reporting on scrap, labor efficiency, spending and continuous improvement savings, and ensures the site has strong controls in partnership with accounting team.
Position location: Butler, Indiana
RESPONSIBLIITIES:
What you will be doing
Lead reporting and financial analysis of manufacturing expenses, providing actionable insights to support cost control, operational efficiency, and profitability objectives.
Develop, monitor, and report key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure operational and financial performance, enabling data-driven decision making, and drive corrective actions with plant leadership.
Create and develop the annual plant budgets and monthly forecasts
Evaluate and communicate periodic actual plant results compared to budgets, forecasts and prior periods.  With a focus primarily on variance reporting, and productivity metrics
Lead standard plant cost and overhead development, including plant cost structure
Manage the monthly and Y/E financial closing process by reviewing and analyzing key plant activity, costs, performance vs. forecast/operating plan.
Partner with the Inventory team to assess financial impacts related to inventory management, including obsolete and excess inventory analysis, and drive mitigation efforts with Product Management, Manufacturing, and cross-functional Therma-Tru teams.
Lead and develop Financial Analysts while partnering with plant leadership to reconcile and analyze daily production metrics, including scrap, labor efficiency, and operational performance drivers.
Coordinate with the Outdoors team in Therma Tru to ensure proper financial reporting, SOX controls, and audit support within the manufacturing site.
Partner with Operations to identify, evaluate, and develop continuous improvement initiatives, conducting monthly cost walks to quantify operational impacts and communicate financial results through the P&L.
Perform ad hoc tasks, including special projects, analysis, and communication as needed to support operations.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, or related field required
5+ years of progressive finance experience within manufacturing, plant, or cost accounting.
Team supervisory or management experience preferred.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Continuously seeks opportunities to enhance knowledge and processes
Experience supporting and driving lean projects.
Hands-on experience with standard costing, including building labor and overhead rates, running or supporting a cost roll, and analyzing manufacturing variances (material, labor, overhead, PPV)
Working knowledge of inventory accounting, including physical counts, cycle counts, and excess, obsolete and slow-moving reserves
Key Skills and Attributes
Strong business partner who is credible on the plant floor and with senior leadership
Explains the “why” behind the numbers clearly and simply
Curious and hands-on: walks the floor, asks questions, follows the data
Takes ownership and drives results, with a bias for action
Can push back respectfully and hold a firm position on numbers and controls
Organized, manages deadlines and works well under month-end pressure

title: Manager, Product Integrity — Connected Products
description:
Fortune Brands Innovations (NYSE: FBIN) is an industry-leading home, security and digital products company with a portfolio of trusted brands, including Moen, House of Rohl, Therma-Tru, Larson, Master Lock, Yale residential, and Sentry Safe.

Fortune Brands Innovations is hiring a Manager, Product Integrity to join our Connected Products team .  Product Integrity is the team that confirms our connected products — Flo by Moen water devices, Yale and August smart locks, and Master Lock connected padlocks — do what their requirements say they do before they reach a customer. This role leads that team and owns the bridge between requirements and proof: taking what Product, Systems Architecture, and Compliance ask for and turning it into tests with a method, a sample size, and a pass/fail criterion.
The role also owns 100% end-of-line testing at the factory, including test fixture design and test software. Depending on test complexity, fixtures are built fully in-house or developed with a supplier.
We are looking for a systems architect who leads a test team . The right person understands the whole product — electrical, mechanical, firmware, and how they interact — well enough to argue a requirement with Product, an interface with Architecture, and the statistics with Reliability, and then run the lab that proves it.
Position location: this position is eligible to work in a hybrid environment out of our North Olmsted, OH or San Francisco, CA locations.
What you will own
The Product Integrity team. Lead a team of test engineers covering production and 100% test, hardware test, reliability test, quality inspection, and overall confirmation of product requirements. You set the direction and the standard; the team executes.
Requirements into tests. Turn every hardware requirement in the PRD — from Product, Systems Architecture, and Compliance — into a testable requirement with a method, a sample size, an acceptance criterion, and a gate. Product defines the design envelope; you define how we test to it.
Gate evidence. Every stage gate (EVT, DVT, PVT) carries your evidence package: what was tested, against which requirement, with what result.
Reliability. Define the reliability test plan for each program and own the statistics behind it: sample sizes, confidence levels, and acceleration factors for environmental testing.
Production test. Develop fixtures and test software that meet approved cycle times, with test limits tied to expected field performance.
Field performance. Review returns and field data, and feed what you learn back into requirements and test plans.
The team and the logistics
Team: test engineers covering production test, hardware test, reliability test, and quality inspection. The lab is in North Olmsted.
Location: North Olmsted, OH or San Francisco, CA. If based in San Francisco, expect occasional travel to North Olmsted.
Travel: ~15%. Travel to factories in Nogales and Tecate, Mexico; Hanoi, Vietnam; and between North Olmsted and San Francisco.
Qualifications
10+ years on connected consumer hardware spanning electrical, mechanical, and firmware.
Experience developing factory test fixtures at both board level and end of line.
Experience writing requirements and V&V plans.
Reliability engineering fluency: accelerated life testing, Weibull and AFR math, sample sizing at a stated confidence, HALT/HASS, thermal, drop, and cycle life. You can design a plan and read a failure.
Production test experience: fixtures, test software, DFT, cycle time, and yield at a contract manufacturer.
Has led a small technical team and is comfortable setting direction for test engineers who are more hands-on than you.
Nice to have
Battery power model development.
Sensor products with calibration and drift requirements.
Sealed or outdoor enclosures.
RF performance characterization.
Certification literacy across safety (UL), RF (FCC), and interop (Matter/CSA); NSF/IAPMO for water products or BHMA for locks.

At Google, we have the good fortune to have developed many interesting systems ranging from planet-spanning databases to near real-time scalable data warehousing to fault-tolerant datastream joining . In SRE, we flip between the fine-grained detail of disk driver I/O scheduling to the big picture of continental-level service capacity, across a range of systems and a user population measured in billions. We own those products in production. We drive reliability and performance across massive scale by mastering the full depth of the stack. We literally do learn something new every day - usually surprising things - that have the potential to transform the lives of billions of our users around the world.

As a member of the Global Communications & Public Affairs team, you will work cross-functionally to help communicate with journalists and other thought leaders; devise specific communications materials and campaigns based on understanding of journalists' interests; engage in face-to-face meetings with commentators and other opinion formers; develop print and web-based material supporting these campaigns; and counter misinformation that might interfere with our business and ability to serve our users. We're looking for great communicators who can understand complex issues and explain them in person and also via well written, simple blog posts, FAQs, video scripts and more.
As a leader, you will keep your team on track with the overall strategy, giving them direction when it comes to specific product and business area decisions. You will also provide direct communications support for senior executives.
We’re looking for a communications leader to join YouTube’s Internal and Executive Communications team. In this role, you’ll be a strategic partner to YouTube's executive leaders, leading a team that focuses on creative and strategic communications in specific product areas and across the company. You will help leaders across Product, Engineering, UX and Trust and Safety communicate the company’s strategy to their teams and the wider Google audience. You should be a great communicator, who can understand complex issues, break them down, and coach executives to then communicate them. Your work ensures alignment across YouTube's product and engineering organizations through strategic storytelling and high-impact internal events.
Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.
US: $171000 - $247000 (USD) + 20% bonus target + equity + benefits

Manage, mentor, and develop a high-performing team. Foster a collaborative, and growth-oriented environment.
Lead proactive and reactive communications plans for sensitive topics, including reorganizations and leadership transitions.
