title: Global Strategic Sourcing Manager
description:
Job Description:
Company description
ITW (NYSE: ITW) is a Fortune 200 global multi-industry manufacturing leader. Its seven industry-leading segments apply the differentiated ITW Business Model to deliver growth, strong margins and attractive returns in markets requiring innovative, customer-focused solutions.
This role is within the Global Weigh & Wrap Division, part of the ITW Food Equipment Segment. The division designs and manufactures commercial weighing and wrapping equipment and software solutions for grocery, retail and food service customers worldwide, under the Avery Berkel and Hobart brands.
The role
The Global Strategic Sourcing Manager is a key member of the Global Weigh & Wrap leadership team and reports to the Vice President and General Manager. The role partners with global business, engineering, operations and materials teams to deliver growth, profitability, supply continuity and product-development objectives.
The position has responsibility for approximately $30 million of global spend, with significant focus on component, electrical and electronic categories. It supports manufacturing operations and new product development in Troy and Hillsboro, Ohio, and Birmingham, United Kingdom, while collaborating across ITW to leverage scale, capability and best practice.
Your responsibilities
•  Develop, implement and continuously improve global sourcing processes, category strategies and supplier strategies aligned with the division’s commercial, operational and technology priorities. Develop annual and long range sourcing plans.
•  Build and maintain a high-quality pipeline of sourcing and productivity opportunities, identifying, managing and delivering sustainable cost reductions, cost avoidance and value improvement.
•  Lead global and regional tenders, supplier selection, qualification and negotiations, including pricing, commercial terms, contracts, quality expectations and supply commitments.
•  Use total-cost analysis, target costing, benchmarking, market intelligence, tariff impact and competitive analysis to improve sourcing decisions and commercial outcomes.
•  Conduct global benchmarking of suppliers, products, technologies and alternative solutions, together with make-or-buy, outsourcing and low-cost-country sourcing assessments where appropriate.
•  Optimise the global supplier base and develop strategic supplier relationships that improve cost, quality, delivery, innovation and responsiveness. Establish and execute clear global supplier standards and governance.
•  Lead the division’s supplier risk and resilience strategy, identifying, assessing and mitigating risks relating to capacity, financial health, geopolitical exposure, commodities, lend of life, technology and continuity of supply.
•  Ensure sourcing strategies balance competitive cost, material availability, inventory, quality and operational resilience; work with materials teams on Kanban, vendor-managed inventory and pull-system opportunities.
•  Provide market, commodity and supplier intelligence to leadership and cross-functional teams, translating external developments into clear risks, opportunities and recommended actions.
•  Partner with Engineering, Operations and New Product Development teams from concept through commercialisation, engaging suppliers early to optimise design, cost, quality, technology, manufacturability, phase in/out and supply continuity.
•  Align sourcing and supplier strategies with current and future product requirements, including component standardisation, preferred technologies and long-term supply roadmaps.
•  Coordinate cross-region and international sourcing projects, promoting standardised processes, common specifications, synergies and leverage across the division and wider ITW organisation.
•  Ensure sourcing activities comply with ITW policies, procedures, ethical standards and contractual requirements, while maintaining appropriate commercial and supplier documentation.
•  Maintain accurate supplier, spend, savings and performance data; develop and monitor dashboards that clearly communicate project status, sourcing performance, risks and results.
•  Provide sourcing leadership, coaching and functional support to local procurement and materials teams, helping strengthen capability, consistency and execution across the division.
Qualifications
•  Bachelor’s degree in business, supply chain management, materials management, engineering or a related discipline; an MBA, advanced technical degree or recognized purchasing qualification is preferred.
•  More than five years of progressive experience in strategic sourcing, procurement or supply chain within an industrial manufacturing environment; experience in capital equipment, machinery, assembly or electrical/electronic components is strongly preferred.
•  Demonstrated experience developing category and supplier strategies, project management, leading formal sourcing processes and delivering measurable cost, quality, delivery and risk improvements in a global environment.
•  Strong negotiation and influencing skills, with sound knowledge of contract development, commercial terms, supplier agreements and procurement risk management.
•  Practical understanding of manufacturing operations, logistics, material requirements planning, inventory management and Lean methods, including Kanban, vendor-managed inventory and pull systems.
•  Experience using total-cost and target-costing methods, supplier and product benchmarking, make-or-buy analysis and market or commodity intelligence.
•  Strong technical, conceptual and analytical capability, with the ability to understand complex products, cost drivers, supply markets and operational trade-offs.
•  Proven ability to lead through influence and work effectively with diverse, international and cross-functional teams, including Engineering, Operations, Quality, Finance and New Product Development.
•  Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to build relationships, challenge constructively and communicate clear recommendations to senior leadership and suppliers.
•  Highly self-motivated, action-oriented and results-focused, with the judgement to set priorities, manage multiple initiatives and follow through to completion.
•  Proficiency in Microsoft Office and experience with ERP, sourcing, spend-analysis and supplier-performance systems.
Working conditions
•  Office-based role either in Troy or Hillsboro, Ohio.
•  Domestic and international travel of approximately 25%, based on business and supplier requirements.

title: AI/ML Engineer Intern
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
The Global Access, Value and Economics (GAVE) organization at Intuitive is seeking a highly motivated, hard-working, and professional AI/ML Engineer Intern to join our team for Summer 2027. The AI/ML Engineer Intern will support GAVE’s mission of generating clinical evidence to drive the adoption of robotic-assisted surgery. They will work within the Global Access and Evidence Management Center of Excellence to develop a system to optimize evidence management and synthesis processes. They will design a tool to identify, deduplicate, validate, and ingest new publications related to Intuitive products. They will also work with the team to integrate existing large language model (LLM) pipelines into this solution. The intern will get hands-on experience with software development, data management, machine learning, and systems design thinking. Beyond technical skills, this internship will require effective communication with numerous cross-functional stakeholders.
Essential Job Duties
Design an end-to-end data pipeline to optimize critical evidence management, synthesis, and generation processes.
Implement and automate publication search and deduplication strategies.
Assist in integrating additional large language model (LLM) workflows into this system.
Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders to develop the solution.
Present and interpret findings to a broad range of teams across the organization.
Required Skills and Experience
Self-motivated individual with a strong interest in data science and machine learning.
Proven ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and address the needs of multiple stakeholders.
Excellent mix of communication and technical skills to engage effectively across all audiences.
Self-driven problem solver who can work with minimal supervision.
Strong desire to learn and grow in the field of data science and machine learning.
Proficiency with Python programming language.
Strong understanding of relational databases and SQL.
Solid grasp of machine learning concepts and algorithms.
Understanding of systems thinking and system design principles.
University Hiring Program Eligibility Requirements:
University Enrollment: Must be currently enrolled in and returning to an accredited degree-seeking academic program after the internship.
Internship Work Period: Must be available to work full-time (approximately 40 hours per week) during a 10–12 week period starting May or June. Specific start dates are shared during the recruiting process.
Internship will be remote/hybrid with opportunity for on-site meetings at a minimum of 3 times during the course of the internship.
Required Education and Training
Current enrollment in a Computer Science, Data Science, Computer Engineering, or related degree-seeking program at the Bachelor’s or Master’s level.
Working Conditions
None
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience with LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, or similar), including prompt engineering and structured outputs.
Experience with Agentic AI workflows.
Experience with building ETL/data ingestion pipelines for Snowflake.
Experience with NLP techniques such as vector embeddings and semantic similarity.
Familiarity with R is a plus.
Experience with scikit-learn is a plus.
Familiarity with statistical methods, systematic literature reviews, and meta-analysis is a plus.

Identify and help remove roadblocks to progress on strategic initiatives, escalating issues appropriately and driving resolution.
Lead special projects and analyses on behalf of the Head of Corporate Strategy as enterprise priorities evolve.

Represent the Head of Corporate Strategy in select meetings and forums, ensuring continuity and consistent messaging across the organization.

Bachelor's degree required; MBA or other advanced degree preferred.
12+ years of progressive professional experience, ideally spanning strategy consulting, corporate strategy, executive or chief-of-staff roles, or an equivalent analytical/operational role, preferably within medical device or broader healthcare industries.
Demonstrated experience operating in a chief-of-staff, executive-office, or similar role supporting senior leaders, ideally within a large, matrixed organization.
Exceptional organizational and program-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams and competing priorities.
Strong executive communication skills, including experience preparing materials for and presenting to senior executives and boards.
Sound judgment and discretion in handling highly sensitive and confidential information.
Proven ability to build trust and influence across a large, matrixed organization without relying on formal authority.
Strong written synthesis skills; able to distill complex, ambiguous information into clear, decision-ready recommendations.
High degree of professional judgment, integrity, and ownership.

title: Director, US Cardiac Marketing
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
The Director, Cardiac Market Development, is a regional leadership role that collaborates closely with the Cardiac Sales Director in US by translating global cardiac procedure and product strategies into market-ready plans, programs, and tools. This role also serves as the US implementation partner to the Vice President, US Cardiac, helping bring key global programs, training processes, and global KOL development initiatives to life across markets with different customer needs, operating models, and development stages.
Working closely with the Cardiac Sales Director and the VP of Cardiac, this role localizes global programs and content, supports training and KOL development execution, tracks performance metrics, and improves quality and matrix efficiency. Commercial priorities and Market-level decisions remain with the US VP of Marketing and the Global Cardiac Vice President and this role is accountable for enabling and accelerating their execution.
Roles & Responsibilities:
Regional Procedure and Product Lifecycle Strategy
Support the Cardiac Sales Directors and VP, Cardiac in developing and executing cardiac procedure strategies using market insights, customer needs, competitive dynamics, clinical pathways, and commercial priorities.
Translate global portfolio, product launch, lifecycle, and procedure strategies into focused roadmaps, priorities, and activation plans.
Coordinate with sales, clinical, capital, key accounts, customer training, marketing, market access, regulatory, and enabling functions to support readiness, sequencing, and execution.
Identify adoption barriers, unmet needs, and growth opportunities and convert them into recommendations and action plans for the Cardiac Sales Directors and VP, Cardiac.
Provide structured feedback to global teams on US/Canada Market requirements, customer needs, evidence gaps, positioning, and future portfolio opportunities.
Market Development and Marketing Localization
Localize cardiac marketing programs, value propositions, messaging, content, media, and field tools consistent with US Marketing Standards, while maintaining brand, clinical, regulatory, and legal requirements.
Provide direct leadership to the US Cardiac marketing manager and plan for clinical marketing team expansion aligned to market growth.
Develop integrated market development plans spanning segmentation, account activation, peer education, society engagement, digital channels, and stakeholder awareness.
Enable teams to build sustainable programs with surgeons, care teams, hospital leaders, key opinion leaders, training centers, and reference sites.
Ensure content and media plans are insight-led, audience-specific, reusable, and aligned to the customer journey and sales execution needs.
Capture, codify, and scale effective practices and share US learnings with other regional marketing leaders, the VP, Global Cardiac, and other Global partners.
Program Support, Metrics, and Operating Cadence
Support the operating rhythm for cardiac Market development and marketing, including annual planning, quarterly business reviews, initiative tracking, and performance reporting.
Define leading and lagging indicators for program effectiveness, adoption progress, launch readiness, content utilization, and return on investment.
Work with FSO to create dashboards and decision forums that help leaders assess progress, resolve barriers, redirect low-value work, and scale successful programs.
Support initiative portfolio tracking by clarifying owners, milestones, dependencies, risks, and expected outcomes.
Support budget planning, tracking, and forecasting for cardiac Market development and marketing programs, in partnership with the Cardiac Sales Directors, VP US Marketing, and VP, Global Cardiac.
Quality, Process, and Matrix Effectiveness
Design scalable processes, standards, and ways of working that increase execution quality, speed, consistency, and accountability.
Clarify interfaces and handoffs across Global, Regional, and local Market teams to reduce duplication, scale best practices, close gaps, and improve matrix efficiency.
Establish quality controls for plans, programs, content, metrics, and launch deliverables, so work is compliant, decision-ready, and fit for use.
Facilitate cross-functional problem-solving and remove barriers that limit field execution or customer impact.
Contribute to a culture of disciplined experimentation, learning, and continuous improvement using data and field feedback.
Partnership and Collaboration
Act as the US point of contact for the VP, Global Cardiac on implementation of key global society initiatives, programs, training curricula, and global KOL development initiatives.
Capitalize on synergies with US Thoracic Marketing Team to maximize opportunities at accounts, society meetings, and other marketing plans.
Serve as a close working partner to the Cardiac Sales Directors in each Market on execution of growth priorities, programs, and training, with market commercial decisions remaining with the Sales Directors and VP/General Managers.
Partner with US commercial teams to drive alignment through influence and collaboration.
Act as the US point of contact for the VP, Global Cardiac on implementation of key global society initiatives, programs, training curricula, and global KOL development initiatives.
Communicate progress, insights, and performance clearly to the Cardiac Sales Directors, VPs/GM US, and the VP Global Cardiac.
Skills, Experience, Education, & Training:
·       Bachelor's degree in business, marketing, life sciences, healthcare, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
·       15+ years of progressive experience in medical devices, healthcare, or another complex regulated industry, including experience in sales, marketing, market development, or commercial operations.
·       Demonstrated success translating global strategies into market-specific cardiac commercial plans and measurable execution and scaling best practices across multiple regions.
·       Experience with procedure development, product launch and lifecycle management, customer segmentation, integrated marketing, and commercial planning.
·       Strong business and financial acumen, including budget tracking, forecasting support, and performance management.
·       Proven ability to lead through influence across functions, and organizational levels in a complex matrix.
·       Advanced analytical capability, including defining metrics, leading operating reviews, interpreting results, and turning insights into decisions.
·       Strong process design, program management, and continuous improvement capability.

Interface and associate with end-user customers in multiple international markets to gather design insights in a highly professional manner, during complex workflow-oriented usability formative study and user research activities.

Prepare and review documentation for submission to regulatory agencies and notified bodies, including supporting the response to questions for additional justification and rationale

Demonstrated experience in HF (UX) and User Research project management.
Demonstrated experience of successful execution or direct support of global regulatory submissions.

human factors (e.g. IEC 62366, AAMI HE75, FDA Applying Human Factors and Usability Engineering to Medical Devices) and advise management regarding potential improvements to internal processes and regulatory issues related to usability engineering.
Excellent verbal communication and presentation skills working within a highly statured communication environment using multiple communication channels (email, text, video conference, instant messaging platforms).

Demonstrated ability to advocate and effectively champion user-centered design and usability engineering principles to product research, development, and design in a fast-paced product development environment.

description:

Primary Function
The Senior Human Factors Engineer works closely with designers, clinical engineers, and technical product managers to inform and guide the development of new products and ensure that those products are safe and easy to use. As part of new product development projects, they conduct user research, analyze and characterize use-related risks, and conduct usability testing of products prior to launch. They have primary responsibility for creating usability risk analyses and conducting final usability validation studies. The Senior Human Factors Engineer also works closely with the regulatory group to create the usability engineering documentation
required for submission to medical device regulatory agencies.
Roles & Responsibilities:
Collect and synthesize detailed information on how users interact with Intuitive products through various techniques including interviews, simulations, direct observations, task analyses, and persona development.
Present results of field observations, research, and usability testing.
Contribute to user interface designs by negotiating design recommendations to mitigate use errors and improve usability. Assist creation and revision of user-interface requirements documents.
Analyze complaints from on-market products and update usability risk assessment and escalate usability-related issues as necessary.
Design, execute, and report on usability (human factors) tests at various stages of product development from early prototypes all the way through formal FDA-mandated validation testing.
Write and execute usability test protocols. Analyze test data and write test reports.
Develop validation strategies for projects involving updates to existing products.
Lead the efforts required to create and update usability risk analyses for Intuitive products
Maintain traces between use risks, mitigations, and validation test cases.
Reinforce a human centered design approach across the organization.
Represent the Human Factors function on core teams for large projects.
Coordinate human factors efforts across projects involving several sub-systems.
Manage usability engineering activities within development projects and provide schedules and status to technical product managers and engineering project managers.
Mentor junior human factors engineers (e.g. interns) and others in organization in usability engineering methods and best practices, as well as Intuitive product development processes.
Prepare and review documentation for submission to regulatory agencies and notified bodies.
Answer questions and provide additional justification and rationale to any questions received.
Keep abreast of regulations and best practices for medical device human factors (e.g. IEC 62366, AAMI HE75, FDA Applying Human Factors and Usability Engineering to Medical Devices) and advise management regarding potential improvements to internal processes and regulatory issues related to usability engineering.
Qualifications
Skills, Experience, Education, & Training:
Minimum BS in Human Factors Engineering, Cognitive Psychology, Computer Science with human-computer interface (HCI) emphasis, Human Centered Design, or related field. MS strongly preferred.
Minimum 8+ years relevant Human Factors/Usability Engineering experience in hardware product development industry
Experience in medical device, or similar regulated industry, a significant plus
Ability to lead usability engineering activities (i.e. establishing usability requirements; creating usability risk analyses, test protocols, and test reports) for a complex, software-controlled electro-mechanical medical device
Ability to interface with customers in a highly professional manner
Ability to analyze and synthesize large quantities of information into usable communications
Superior ability to write accurate, clear, and concise protocols, reports, operating procedures, etc. in a timely manner
Excellent verbal communication and presentation skills
Ability to work with and across various groups and levels of management within the organization, including other engineering groups, marketing, clinical engineering, and regulatory. Excellent collaboration skills.
Ability to apply user-centered design and usability engineering principles to product research, development, and design
Ability to travel internationally as well as domestically (up to 25%)

Drive periodic review/ clean-up actions for NPI planning material in the NPI locations

Rigor in operational excellence, projects and initiatives to drive business outcomes.

·         Excellent verbal, written, presentation, executive communication skills and the ability to interact professionally with a diverse group of internal customers.

·         Masters or BS degree or equivalent.
·         12+ years of experience in Production Planning, Demand/Supply planning, Purchasing, Inventory Management domains
·         5+ years of experience in directly managing high performing teams.
·         Multi-plant work experience highly desired

~20% travel to both domestic and international operating sites.

Experience working in medium to large medical device manufacturing organizations within multinational and cross-matrixed management settings.
Masters level degree in engineering, supply chain/business management, finance discipline.
·         Significant experience with core business systems including SAP, Agile, advanced planning solutions

Analyze complex electro-mechanical devices for dynamic safety and clinical risk.
Apply control theory to the design and verification of mechatronic and tele-robotic systems.
Integrate prototype hardware with existing systems.
Develop and implement motion control and safety algorithms, including documentation of risks, requirements, and test protocols.
Develop cartesian controls for manipulator robotics to design and implement precise and efficient robotic movements.
Participate in clinical observations and experiments to ensure that performance requirements are relevant and realistic.
Communicate system performance to the organization.
Support and track system performance as it evolves from design engineering to manufacturing.
Provide analytical assistance and tool building for other engineering issues.

Document and communicate intellectual property.

Minimum MS degree in CS, ME, EE, or similar with 4–5+ years of industrial experience or PhD with 1–3+ years of experience.

Possess MATLAB and Python programming capabilities, as well as hardware and software integration skills.
Be detail-oriented and able to develop and drive a single solution to completion.
Comfort with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, and risk analysis.
Hands-on engineering experience with proven ability to work well in a team environment.
Self-motivated and proactive in engaging with interdisciplinary teams to address and solve complex problems.

Job Purpose
To ensure we are supplying customers with the highest quality products while adhering to all food and safety standards. This is accomplished by batching food product/condiments to corporate/customer approved recipes.
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
• Obtains instruction from lead processor or supervisor.
• Ability to follow complete production schedules with minimal scrap/spoilage
• Keep up with volume of work required
• Visually inspects equipment at station for cleanliness or obvious maintenance problems.
• Cleans small machine components, as needed.
• Reports any problems to lead processor or supervisor.
• Makes piping connections as needed for particular process on schedule.
• Monitors equipment controls, temperature meters, valves and adjusts as needed.
• Operates forklift/pallet jack to obtain ingredients or move pallets/totes in and around processing area.
• While slow, assists processing assistants in cleaning processing areas by scrubbing walls, hosing floor, sweeping floor/emptying trash and performing other cleaning duties.
• Utilizes can openers, knives, band cutters, snips, pliers and other small items to open ingredient cases/packages.
• Maintains neat work area. Wipes spills that have occurred during mixing process.
• Records data pertaining to work completed, ingredients used, lot codes and other processing information.
• Assists in cleaning equipment and lines between recipes.
• Very occasionally obtains ingredients/supplies from warehouse.
• Obtains samples of batches and taste test.
• Asks lead, supervisor or material handler if there is any rework.
• Uses rework if there is any consistently.
• Determines ingredients required for formula/recipe and the required amount.
• Ability to safely lift 50lbs on a regular basis.
• Obtains ingredients from storage area or around work area and pours into kettle.
• Meters in other ingredients as required by watching meters and turning on/off kettle.
• Utilizes drum lift by strapping drum into lift and operating hydraulic lift with chain.
• Manually pushes drum lift to kettle and dumps drum of ingredients as needed.
• Operates controls to activate mixers and equipment.
• Monitors controls, equipment temperature, valves, and adjusts equipment to meet formula requirements.
• Hoses spills off floor and hoses towards drains.
• Obtains, measures and weighs additional ingredients to set aside in preparation for next batch or recipe.
• Assists other processors in pouring ingredients into kettles as needed.
• Collects samples and tests for pH, acidity, viscosity and solids.
• Reads test results and adjusts equipment/recipe accordingly.

Job Description
As a Sr. Scientist within the Process Technology group in R&D Central Processing you will serve as a technical processing expert responsible for exploring and developing new process technologies, building our internal processing capabilities, and hands-on execution of complex, high-impact processing projects from concept through commercialization. You will own the technical delivery of assigned initiatives, partnering closely with cross-functional stakeholders to translate processing concepts into manufacturable, Right-First-Time solutions.​
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
​​Identify, evaluate, and prioritize emerging process technologies (equipment, automation, digital, etc) aligned to business needs.
​Develop scale up strategies from prototyping to pilot plant, and right the first time commercialization to drive optimal project execution.
​Execute end-to-end technical delivery across assigned complex processing projects, including technical briefing, concept development, technical design, learning plans, pilot runs, capital design, and commercialization handover to Operations/Supply Chain.
​Develop and maintain detailed technical documentation including Manufacturing Procedure Specifications, Transformation Flowsheets, and Process Design Scopes, ensuring processing parameters meet defined quality, shelf-life, consumer experience, and manufacturing performance requirements.
​Apply processing commercialization tools (CQV, FMEA, CPRA) to systematically identify and mitigate technical risks, drive design decisions, and ensure Right-First-Time launch readiness.
​Partner with Platform R&D, GDI R&D, Packaging R&D, Quality, Operations, and external suppliers to define processing requirements and success criteria, resolve technical trade-offs, and maintain project timelines and milestones.
​Lead and support pilot line trials and scale-up activities, translating learnings into robust commercial processing solutions.
​Contribute to STAR and Tech Review Board processes, preparing and presenting technical content that clearly communicates design rationale, risk status, and commercialization readiness.
​Maintain compliance with all regulatory and safety requirements throughout project execution.
​Support cost optimization and value engineering efforts that improve margin, sustainability, and reinvestment priorities.
​Serve as an informal technical mentor to junior processing engineers on the team, sharing applied expertise and supporting capability development.​
Key Outputs & Deliverables
Deliver successful technical execution across concurrent complex processing projects within innovation and platform portfolios, meeting committed timelines, budgets, and technical performance targets.
Achieve and sustain >95% Right-First-Time (RTF) launches across assigned projects, ensuring processing solutions meet manufacturability, quality, regulatory, and supply chain readiness criteria at first commercial production.
Produce high-quality processing technical deliverables — including Manufacturing Procedure Specifications, Transformation Flowsheets, Process Design Scopes, FMEAs, and CQV documentation — that meet enterprise engineering standards.
Generate clear, data-driven technical recommendations and risk assessments that enable informed go/no-go decisions at governance milestones.
Contribute to team capability by sharing technical learnings, best practices, and processing expertise across the broader E2E projects organization.
Expected Experience & Required Skills
​​BS/MS/PhD degree in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or related discipline.
​Minimum 4 years of experience in R&D or Engineering roles within consumer goods, food & beverage, pharma, or a similar industry.
​Demonstrated experience in emulsions / shear processing, fermentation, extrusion, thermal processing & validation, aeration, drying, or powder mixing preferred.
​Demonstrated hands-on experience executing end-to-end processing development projects, including pilot trials and scale-up to industrial production.
​Strong applied knowledge of processing commercialization tools including CQV, FMEA, CPRA, Process Design Scopes, and Transformation Flowsheets.
​Solid project management skills, with experience maintaining detailed project plans, schedules, and risk logs on multi-stakeholder initiatives.
​Proficiency with project tools (MS Project, Smartsheet, Jira, or equivalent), advanced Excel skills; familiarity with ERP systems (SAP).
​Strong technical communication skills with the ability to synthesize complex processing data into clear recommendations for cross-functional audiences.
​Experience with pilot line setup, scale-up, and industrial production launches, including multi-site experience preferred.
​Willingness and ability to travel up to 25% of the time.​

title: Analyst, Procurement & Material Planning - Packaging
description:
Job Description:
Analyst, Procurement & Material Planning – Packaging
Location: Salt Lake City, UT
Hybrid: 3 days/week in-office
About Us
Established in 2017, Trü Frü changed the way America snacks forever. We are a Utah-based company that rapidly ascended the permissible indulgence space by innovating a better-for-you snack containing 100% real fruit immersed in premium chocolate. We are on an exciting mission to build a fruit-forward snacking legacy around an incredible product line with trüly remarkable people to create something special for generations to come!
What You'll Do
As the Material Planning – Packaging Analyst , you'll keep Trü Frü's material supply steady across our network of co-manufacturers and suppliers. You'll forecast, plan and manage raw material inventory to support production, hit safety stock targets and minimize waste.
Responsibilities
Develop and maintain planning tools to track packaging material inventory across a multi-site, multi-brand, multi-vendor network.
Recommend network-wide packaging material safety stock targets, replenishment processes and KPIs.
Issue monthly and ad hoc forecasts to suppliers and internal stakeholders
Review packaging inventory with Procurement and communicate updates to co-manufacturers.
Provide packaging waste risk analysis for Finance accruals.
Track packaging changes to keep obsolescence within budget, flagging outliers to the cross-functional team.
Lead packaging supply strategy for new co-manufacturing sites, building best practices with co-man planning counterparts.
Onboard new packaging suppliers, setting a clear forecast cadence for their capacity planning.
Initiate in-network material transfers to reduce obsolescence and shortage risk
Act as liaison between co-manufacturers, suppliers and internal teams (Manufacturing, Procurement, Supply Planning, Quality) to keep supply on target.
Run "what if" scenario planning on demand shifts to guide purchasing decisions.
Participate in supplier QBRs and maintain packaging strategy documents (lead times, MOQs, shelf life).
Manage materials inputs in Trü Frü systems (Blue Yonder, SAP, Reltio, etc.)
Document processes in SOPs and train new team members.
Develop and maintain tools to efficiently track and manage packaging material requirements across multiple contract manufacturers, ensuring material availability to support production and business needs.
Support material planning and purchase order management for new product launches, ensuring timely material availability to meet commercialization and production timelines.
Skills and Experience
3+ years in material or supply planning.

title: Learning Business Partner
description:
Job Description:
The Learning Business Partner acts as a strategic co-pilot and advisor to senior business leaders, driving organizational performance by translating complex business strategies into sustainable capability architectures.
This role owns the end-to-end learning value chain—from strategic business relationship management and performance consulting to learning needs analysis, high-level learning solution design, and evaluation. This role creates high-impact capability strategies and designs holistic learning experiences that seamlessly integrate into the daily flow of work, directly enabling business growth and Associate skill building
Key Responsibilities
1. Performance Consulting & Stakeholder Relationship Management (Consulting & Influence)
·         Strategic Business Partnership: Act as the primary interface and trusted advisor to stakeholders. Proactively manage senior stakeholder relationships, establishing credibility to influence decision-making and champion the enterprise learning agenda.
·         Performance Diagnostics: Use advanced performance consulting methodologies to diagnose organizational performance challenges. Conduct root-cause analyses to distinguish between training opportunities and other organizational, process, or talent-related interventions.
·         Demand & Portfolio Management: Effectively manage and prioritize the pipeline of learning requests. Act as a strategic gateway, aligning proposed learning solutions with key business priorities and long-term talent strategies.
2. Learning Needs Analysis & Capability Architecture (Skills & Learning Strategy)
·         Diagnostic Skills Assessment: Apply quantitative and qualitative research methodologies (surveys, data benchmarks, focus groups, interviews) to map existing skills inventories, isolate skill gaps, and define the critical capabilities required for future-readiness.
·         Capability & Skills Architecture: Design and maintain agile skills matrices and capability frameworks aligned with business strategies. Define current versus ideal performance states and design scalable learning pathways to close the gap.
·         Enterprise Synergy: Collaborate across functional domains to identify horizontal capability trends, scaling successful learning models and preventing fragmented, redundant initiatives.
3. Holistic Learning Solution Design (Design & Orchestration)
·         High-Level Solution Design: Map human-centered learner journeys and establish robust instructional design frameworks. Architect multi-faceted learning ecosystems that integrate formal, social, and experiential (70/20/10) learning components.
·         Modality & Technology Selection: Evaluate and select optimal delivery formats (digital self-paced, synchronous virtual, classroom, social learning networks, or workflow-embedded tools) that maximize engagement and drive behavioral change.
·         ID Partnering & Quality Assurance: Define and document high-level design specifications and standards for external and internal Instructional Design (ID) partners. Collaborate closely during the build phase, maintaining accountability for the overall design integrity, context alignment, and deployment success.
4. Data Literacy, Measurement, and Impact (Analytics & Valuation)
·         Success Metrics Definition: Define key performance indicators (KPIs) and business impact metrics at the outset of every initiative in collaboration with business sponsors.
·         Measurement & Evaluation: Apply robust evaluation frameworks (e.g., LTEM, Kirkpatrick) to monitor learner engagement, behavior change, and business ROI.
·         Insights-Driven Optimization: Analyze data to derive insights, communicate the strategic value of learning to executive leadership, and continuously optimize the portfolio.
Context and Scope
The Learning Business Partner operates in a fast-paced, highly matrixed, global environment. The role holder must successfully navigate complex stakeholder landscapes across global segments, cultures, and time zones.
The role operates at the critical intersection of business leaders and centralized learning execution teams. Rather than producing raw training content, the Learning Business Partner owns the "What" and "Why “defining the strategic learning agenda and designing the learner experience—while steering the "How" in partnership with Instructional Designers and vendors. The position requires a high degree of autonomy, executive presence, and the ability to influence without authority.

·         Minimum Experience: 8+ years of progressive experience in Learning & Development
·         Global Readiness: Demonstrated capability to operate effectively across diverse geographical regions and cultures. Regular availability to support US/European time zones is required.
·         Travel: Ability to travel up to 10% of the time for key stakeholder alignment meetings and learning forums.
Key Knowledge & Experience
·         Consulting & Influence: Masterful ability to conduct diagnostics, build trusted-advisor relationships, manage expectation mismatches, and influence VP/Director-level stakeholders.
·         Business & Functional Acumen: Deep understanding of corporate structures and business value chains (Sales, Supply, R&D, Finance, P&O, etc.) with the ability to speak the language of business leaders.
·         Digital Fluency & AI Capability: Savviness in utilizing modern learning technology stacks (LMS, LXP, social learning environments) and emerging AI capabilities for automated curation, skill taxonomy tagging, and personalized learning journeys.
·         Data Literacy: Proven experience defining data collection methodologies, reading dashboards, interpreting learner analytics, and synthesizing data points into executive-level narratives.
·         Adult Learning Strategy: Expert-level knowledge of adult learning theories, cognitive design principles, behavioral economics/change management, and 70/20/10 operationalization.
Competency Profile
Key Mars Leadership Competencies
·         Strategic Mindset: Sees ahead to future possibilities and translates them into breakthrough strategies.
·         Balances Stakeholders: Anticipates and balances the needs of multiple stakeholders across a matrix.
·         Collaborates: Builds partnerships and works collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives.
·         Manages Ambiguity: Operates effectively, even when things are not certain or the way forward is unclear.
·         Nimble Learning: Learns quickly when facing new situations, experimenting to find solutions.
·         Plans & Aligns: Plans and prioritizes work to meet commitments aligned with organizational goals.

Job Description:

Segment: Mars Petcare (Greenies)

Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent
Join Our Greenies Team in North Kansas City
At Mars Petcare, we are passionate about pets. Our Greenies brand is dedicated to keeping pets healthy and happy, and we manufacture our world-renowned products right here in our highly desirable, fully climate-controlled North Kansas City facility.
Being a Mars Associate is all about opportunity. The opportunity to do the kind of challenging, interesting work that shapes the world’s best-loved brands. To work with real purpose, supported by talented, friendly people from all sorts of different backgrounds.
Whether you are an experienced warehouse professional, a skilled forklift operator looking for a stable day-shift position, or a transitioning military Veteran, Reservist, or National Guard member, we welcome your unique talents! We highly value the dedication, safety-first mindset, and structured teamwork developed in the military and look forward to helping you build a successful civilian career.
Job Summary
The Material Handler is responsible for the end-to-end logistics flow within our plant. This dual-focus role handles all incoming packaging and raw ingredients, manages safe product movement inside the site, loads outbound trailers for shipment, completes all logistics paperwork, and maintains perfect inventory control. This associate works closely with production, purchasing, receiving, shipping, and quality teams to ensure seamless plant operations in a clean, temperature-controlled environment.
Key Responsibilities
Receiving & Inbound Logistics
Receive and verify all incoming raw materials, ingredients, packaging, and components against purchase orders and shipping manifests.
Use a forklift to safely unload inbound trucks and transfer materials to their correct designated storage locations.
Conduct strict quality and food safety checks on incoming materials, including collecting product samples and verifying supplier paperwork.
Collaborate with external logistics departments and freight carriers to ensure correct and safe delivery of production materials.
Material Handling & Warehouse Operations
Safely and accurately operate material handling equipment (including forklifts) to transport inventory, raw materials, WIP (work-in-process), and finished goods throughout the facility.
Support production schedules by ensuring that the correct materials are issued and staged in production areas when needed.
Stage, build, and load outbound trailers for shipment, ensuring proper cargo weight distribution and trailer utilization.
Ensure proper labeling, sorting, FIFO (First-In, First-Out) rotation, and general organization of all materials in storage areas.
Inventory, Systems, & Documentation
Scan and track material movements using warehouse management systems to ensure perfect real-time inventory accountability.
Perform daily cycle counts, participate in precision monthly inventories, and assist with formal physical audits.
Investigate inventory discrepancies promptly and report findings to management.
Generate, review, and complete accurate shipping/receiving paperwork, logging all transactions accurately into the plant database.
Safety, Quality, & Food Safety Culture
Participate and adhere to all food safety requirements, Quality Management Processes (QMPs), and site safety programs, championing a safety-first culture.
Maintain a clean, organized, and sanitary warehouse environment in accordance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs).
Promptly report any safety, food safety, or quality concerns to leadership.
Position Requirements
Minimum Qualifications:
Education: High school diploma, GED, or equivalent civilian/military education.
Experience: Proven experience in warehouse logistics, receiving, shipping, or material handling roles.
Equipment: Demonstrated experience operating a forklift safely in an industrial or warehouse environment.
Physical Ability: Must be in good physical condition with the ability to stand and walk for extended periods, bend, reach, climb, and safely lift up to 40 pounds manually.
Technical Literacy: Working knowledge of basic computer programs for entering data, record keeping, and maintaining inventory logs.
Core Skills: Basic math skills, a keen eye for detail, strong organizational skills, and excellent written and verbal communication abilities.
Teamwork: Demonstrated ability to work in a high-performing team environment with a willingness to learn and be coached.
Military & Veteran Technical Equivalency Guide
At Mars, we recognize that your military service has prepared you to excel in logistical operations. Your training in high-stakes material movement, precision inventory tracking, and supply chain management maps directly to this role. If you served in any of the following specialties, we highly encourage you to apply:
U.S. Army: Automated Logistical Specialist (92A), Unit Supply Specialist (92Y), Cargo Specialist (88H), Motor Transport Operator (88M), Ammunition Specialist (89B). Your experience with warehouse databases, material handling equipment (MHE), and precise property book audits is an excellent fit.

U.S. Air Force: Materiel Management (2S0X1), Traffic Management (2T0X1), Ground Transportation (2T1X1). Your training in cargo loading, receiving inspections, strict compliance with safety procedures, and inventory precision is an exact match.
U.S. Marine Corps: Warehouse Clerk (3051), Supply Administration & Operations (3043), Logistics/Embarkation Specialist (0431), Motor Vehicle Operator (3531). Your focus on cargo staging, load planning, and material handling equipment matches our shipping and receiving operations.
U.S. Coast Guard: Storekeeper (SK), Marine Science Technician.
What We Offer (Total Rewards & Benefits)
At Mars, being an associate is more than a job—it's an opportunity to build a long-term career. We provide a competitive, industry-leading package starting on your very first day:
Compensation: Competitive base pay based on experience, shift differentials, and significant overtime (OT) potential.
Annual Bonus: Eligibility for our annual performance-based company bonus and annual merit increases.
Health & Wellness: Comprehensive Medical, Vision, and Dental insurance starting on Day One.

Family Support: Paid Parental Leave, plus Short-Term and Long-Term Disability.
Career Growth: Access to top-tier learning and development through Mars University.

The Human Genome Project made human protein sequences accessible at scale; AlphaFold did the same for structure prediction. But our understanding biomolecular function is still in its infancy, limiting our ability to develop safe, effective medicines.

description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI Finance is responsible for ensuring the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The Controllership team delivers the financial truth that powers OpenAI’s growth. By translating operational activity into accurate, timely, and decision-grade financial data, we enable leadership to scale the business with confidence. Our commitment to rigorous controls and best-in-class systems ensures financial integrity as OpenAI grows. 

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a strategic and execution-oriented Accounting Lead, Hardware to build and scale inventory accounting capabilities across consumer hardware and robotics businesses. This role partners closely with Finance, Supply Chain, Manufacturing Operations, Technical Accounting, Strategic Finance, and Systems teams to establish scalable inventory and supply chain accounting processes and reporting infrastructure supporting rapid growth and product launches.

The ideal candidate brings strong accounting fundamentals, sound judgment, and a track record of building scalable processes in complex, evolving businesses. Inventory, cost accounting, or supply chain experience is preferred, and accounting experience supporting hardware, infrastructure, data centers, or other capital-intensive operations is also valuable. We welcome strong accounting professionals from other backgrounds who have demonstrated the ability to quickly learn unfamiliar business models and accounting topics and take ownership of new areas. This person should thrive in ambiguity, combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution, and communicate effectively with cross-functional partners and senior leadership.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: 


INVENTORY ACCOUNTING

 - Lead inventory and supply chain accounting across consumer hardware and robotics programs, including inventory valuation, supply chain/sourcing arrangements, manufacturing variances, reserves, and close processes.

 - Partner with Supply Chain, Operations, and Strategic Finance to support BOM accuracy, labor and overhead assumptions, operationalize supply chain strategies and gross margin analysis.

 - Develop scalable accounting processes for NPI, prototyping, engineering builds, and mass production.

 - Own inventory-related accounting policies and controls, including capitalization, overhead allocation, LCNRV/NRV assessments, rebates, freight, tariffs, and inventory controls.


ERP SYSTEMS & PROCESS DESIGN

 - Serve as a finance lead for Oracle Fusion manufacturing costing and inventory implementations, enhancements, and process optimization.

 - Partner with Systems, IT, and Operations to design scalable finance processes, controls, reporting structures, and operational workflows.

 - Partner with Systems and Operations to define accounting requirements and guide ERP design for product costing, inventory transactions, and related reporting and controls.


FINANCIAL CLOSE, REPORTING & CONTROLS

 - Lead monthly, quarterly, and annual cost accounting close activities and improve scalable reconciliations, reporting, and management review processes.

 - Partner with Strategic Finance on margin reporting, inventory analytics, and budget versus actual analysis.

 - Establish SOX-ready controls, support audits and technical accounting matters, and drive continuous improvement across close and reporting processes.


CROSS-FUNCTIONAL LEADERSHIP

 - Act as a strategic partner to Operations, Supply Chain, Procurement, and Program Management teams.

 - Translate ambiguous business needs into scalable accounting and operational frameworks.

 - Influence senior stakeholders through strong communication, executive presence, and data-driven recommendations.

 - Help build and scale the long-term roadmap for hardware controllership, manufacturing accounting, and operational finance infrastructure.

 


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Bring strong accounting judgment and enjoy learning how physical products, infrastructure, and operational workflows translate into financial reporting.

 - Have a track record of quickly developing expertise in unfamiliar accounting areas, asking thoughtful questions, and turning what you learn into practical processes and controls.

 - Can comfortably operate between strategic leadership discussions and highly detailed operational accounting analyses.

 - Have strong executive presence and can communicate effectively with senior leadership and cross-functional partners.

 - Enjoy building scalable processes and infrastructure in fast-moving, ambiguous environments.

 - Are highly detail-oriented and maintain a strong control mindset while balancing business partnership.

 - Have a strong systems orientation and enjoy designing scalable ERP and reporting processes.

 - Are intellectually curious, proactive, and solutions-oriented.

 


QUALIFICATIONS


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

 - 8+ years of progressive accounting experience, with ownership of complex accounting areas, close processes, or operational accounting.

 - Strong understanding of U.S. GAAP and demonstrated ability to research unfamiliar accounting topics and apply sound judgment.

 - Demonstrated ability to quickly learn new business models, systems, and operational processes and take ownership of unfamiliar accounting areas.

 - Experience building or improving accounting processes, reconciliations, controls, and reporting.

 - Strong systems aptitude and experience working with ERP systems and financial data.

 - Excellent analytical, communication, and cross-functional partnership skills.

 - Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders and execute effectively in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Experience in one or more of the following areas is valuable; candidates are not expected to bring all of them:

 - Inventory, cost, manufacturing, or supply chain accounting, including inventory valuation, standard costing, manufacturing variances, overhead allocation, rebates and buy/sell etc.

 - Accounting supporting hardware, infrastructure, data centers, electronics, robotics, semiconductors, or other capital-intensive operations.

 - Work with contract manufacturers, global supply chains, hardware product launches, or manufacturing scale-up.

 - Oracle Fusion, particularly Costing and Inventory modules, or comparable ERP implementation and process improvement experience.

 - CPA and/or public accounting background.

 - Experience in a high-growth technology environment or building and leading accounting teams.

This role will play a foundational part in building the accounting infrastructure that supports the next generation of AI hardware products. You will help shape the systems, policies, controls, and operational processes that enable scalable manufacturing operations, reliable financial reporting, and launch readiness as the business rapidly grows.

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital and delivery partners, is building the infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems. The Data Center Engineering team defines repeatable technical standards and carries them through design, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness. We are seeking a Controls Engineer to design and integrate automation systems for on-site power generation serving large AI data center campuses. You will own control architecture and functional requirements across generation packages, balance-of-plant systems, electrical protection, microgrid controls, and data center monitoring.  - Experience developing functional specifications, sequences, I/O, alarms, graphics, and factory or site test procedures.

 - Ability to troubleshoot across software, instrumentation, electrical, mechanical, communications, and operating-process boundaries.

title: Counsel, AI Safety & Cyber Incident Response
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Legal team helps address the cutting-edge legal questions that arise from developing and deploying advanced AI. The Security and Public Sector Legal team helps protect OpenAI’s technology, systems, data, and people and supports the safe and responsible use of our tools. We work closely with technical and operational teams to provide practical advice on novel, consequential, and fast-moving issues.



About the Role

We are seeking a counsel to help lead legal responses to cybersecurity and AI safety incidents. This is an opportunity to bring deep incident response expertise to some of the hardest questions in AI, and help build the legal frameworks and practices for answering them.



You will advise on complex cybersecurity incidents, from discovery through to resolution, and also help develop our response to incidents involving the safety of our models and tools. AI safety incident response is a new and rapidly evolving legal practice area. Your work will help define how frontier AI companies investigate and respond to safety events such as unexpected model behavior, degradation of safeguards, harmful uses of our services, and potential harm to third parties—often where established legal standards do not yet exist. Working directly with Security, Safety, Product, Engineering, and colleagues across Legal, you will advise on consequential decisions where established approaches may offer little guidance.



We are looking for a practical, dynamic lawyer who can turn incomplete information into clear recommendations, exercise sound judgment on novel questions, and follow matters through to resolution. You will help establish the facts, assess risks, and guide investigations, communications, remediation, and reporting. You will also turn lessons from individual incidents into durable response processes, helping further develop a legal function that evolves alongside the technology.



This role is based in Washington, D.C. or San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.



In this role, you will be:

 - Serving as legal lead on assigned cybersecurity and AI safety incidents, coordinating fact development, legal analysis and advising, cross-functional escalation, and follow-through with the response team.

 - Working with investigators to understand incident scope, attack paths, root cause, and affected systems and data, and potential third-party impacts, while helping teams distinguish established facts from gaps in the evidence.

 - Managing outside counsel and third party service provider engagements necessary to incident response.

 - Serving as key Legal point of contact for cross-functional teams.

 - Partnering with Privacy, Product, Regulatory, and other counsel to assess notification and reporting obligations, advise on timely customer and user communications, and coordinate third-party outreach and incident-related information sharing with industry peers and government partners.

 - Preparing concise incident updates and decision materials that distinguish established facts, uncertainties, options, and recommended next steps.

 - Developing severity-based escalation criteria, response playbooks, exercises, and clear decision and handoff processes for cybersecurity and AI safety incidents, adapting established practices to emerging model risks.

 - Supporting post-incident reviews, tracking agreed corrective actions, and turning lessons into practical improvements to safeguards and response processes.
   
   

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - A JD and a license or qualification to practice law in your jurisdiction.

 - 5+ years of relevant experience.

 - Relevant legal experience managing cybersecurity or privacy incident responses or comparable complex technology investigations at a technology company, law firm, or government agency, including work with technical teams, other counsel, and communications partners.

 - The ability to translate technical findings into practical legal advice, with a working understanding of technical information.

 - Sound judgment under time pressure, clear communication of uncertainty, and an understanding of when to act, seek specialist advice, or escalate.

 - Clear, concise writing and the ability to keep cross-functional teams aligned through changing facts and competing priorities.

 - Ownership of details and follow-through, paired with collaborative work with colleagues who bring different expertise.

 - A strong interest in the novel challenges of AI safety and a willingness to help develop new approaches. Direct AI incident experience is helpful; strong transferable incident response skills are welcome.

 - Availability to participate in time-sensitive incident response, including occasional work outside normal business hours.

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

Experiments make expression, introspective, optimistic, thoughtful, and impactful things with frontier models. Continuing to experiment while pushing the spectrum of what the voice and stories we tell. We bring creative and technical collaborators together to explore what these models make possible through prototypes, interactive experiences, physical objects, and stories that invite people to participate, reflect, and imagine.

title: Data Center Controls Engineer (BMS / EPMS)
description:
About the Team

OpenAI is building the infrastructure foundation for the next generation of AI. The Data Center Engineering team defines the strategy, reference architectures, technical requirements, and delivery standards for the large-scale data centers that support OpenAI research, products, and infrastructure partners.

As a Data Center Controls Engineer, you will program, configure, integrate, and commission the controls systems that support high-density AI data centers. You will work hands-on with mechanical or electrical controls, partnering with mechanical, electrical, IT/networking, security, commissioning, operations, and external delivery teams.

About the Role

We are seeking hands-on, early-career controls engineers with practical experience in building management systems (BMS) and mechanical controls, or electrical power monitoring systems (EPMS) and electrical controls. This role focuses on implementing and commissioning control systems, including PLCs, field devices, instrumentation, and sequences of operation, rather than owning OT/IT network or cybersecurity architecture.

The ideal candidate has day-to-day experience programming and commissioning controls, ideally with a controls systems integrator. We welcome depth in either BMS/mechanical or EPMS/electrical controls; expertise in both is not required. You will work with experienced engineers and delivery partners to turn design requirements into reliable, tested systems.

Key Responsibilities

 - Program and configure PLCs and control systems for mechanical/BMS or electrical/EPMS applications in AI data center campuses.

 - Implement and test sequences of operation, control logic, alarms, and interlocks against approved functional requirements.

 - Review and maintain controls documentation, including control diagrams, I/O and point lists, instrumentation details, sequences of operation, and commissioning records.

 - Integrate field devices, sensors, instrumentation, equipment controllers, and supervisory systems; validate point mapping, communications, and data quality.

 - Maintain control programs, configuration backups, version history, change records, and rollback procedures to support safe commissioning and operations.

 - Partner with mechanical, electrical, IT/networking, cybersecurity, and operations teams to resolve integration issues and implement approved OT connectivity and security requirements.

 - Configure and troubleshoot relevant industrial communications, such as BACnet/IP, BACnet MS/TP, Modbus TCP/RTU, OPC UA, or IEC 61850, according to the system and controls discipline.

 - Work directly with controls integrators, equipment vendors, contractors, and commissioning teams to resolve programming, installation, and functional performance issues.

 - Execute and document factory and site acceptance testing, point-to-point checks, sequence verification, and integrated systems testing; troubleshoot control logic, instrumentation, alarms, and device communication failures.

Qualifications

 - Practical hands-on experience programming, configuring, integrating, or commissioning control systems in data centers, industrial automation, buildings, or other critical infrastructure environments.

 - Working knowledge of PLC programming and control logic, with the ability to implement and troubleshoot sequences of operation.

 - Experience in either BMS/mechanical controls or EPMS/electrical controls, with an understanding of the equipment and operating sequences in that discipline.

 - Experience configuring field devices and instrumentation, validating I/O and point mapping, and diagnosing control system behavior.

 - Working knowledge of relevant industrial communication protocols and basic OT networking needed to connect and troubleshoot control systems.

 - Ability to read control diagrams, equipment documentation, I/O lists, and functional specifications, and keep implementation records accurate.

 - Hands-on experience with functional testing, commissioning, and systematic troubleshooting using trends, alarms, logs, and field observations.

 - Ability to work closely with integrators, vendors, construction teams, and operations, communicate issues clearly, and follow safe work and change-control practices.

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Controls or Automation Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Skills

 - Experience at a controls systems integrator, with regular responsibility for programming, configuration, field integration, and commissioning.

 - Experience delivering BMS/mechanical or EPMS/electrical controls for data centers or other mission-critical facilities.

 - Familiarity with supervisory controls, HMI/SCADA configuration, telemetry, and historian integrations.

 - Familiarity with OT cybersecurity practices and working with networking or security specialists to implement approved access and connectivity requirements.

 - Experience with scripting, APIs, or automation tools that improve controls testing, integration, documentation, or troubleshooting.

Work Environment and Travel

 - This role requires periodic travel to data center campuses, vendors, labs, construction sites, commissioning activities, and controls/network cutovers.

 - The engineer should be comfortable working across office, lab, construction, and live data center environments, including PPE, lockout/tagout, cyber hygiene, and change-control requirements.

 - Work may include time-sensitive support during commissioning, startup, vendor testing, cutovers, network changes, telemetry issues, automation failures, and operational events.

Travel: 50%

The Strategic Finance Data Science team helps OpenAI understand business performance and make informed decisions about growth, revenue, and resource allocation. We partner with Strategic Finance, Data Engineering, and business teams to build trusted metrics, explain what is changing, and support forecasting, planning, pricing, and investment decisions.

You will work across the analytical workflow: define the question, establish trustworthy metrics and datasets, investigate the drivers, and help partners act on the findings.

 - Define and maintain trusted metrics and analytical datasets for revenue, usage, customer performance, compute consumption, and margin, with clear definitions and appropriate product, customer, and cohort detail.

description:

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Designer to lead hands-on design for research and experimental creative work. You’ll help define a project’s visual direction, build prototypes, and carry promising ideas through to finished work across research communications, demos, and experiences.

This role combines strong graphic design craft with an experimental approach to making. You’ll work closely with researchers, creative leads, and production partners, bringing structure to open-ended briefs and helping collaborators turn technical concepts into work people can understand and engage with.

 - Partner with researchers and creative leads to define the design problem, identify the essential story, and establish a clear visual direction.

 - Translate research concepts, methods, and findings into accurate visual narratives, checking interpretations and limitations with subject-matter experts.

 - Own design delivery for complex workstreams, align priorities with partners, and adapt scope as research findings and production requirements evolve.

 - 8+ years of relevant experience

 - A portfolio demonstrating senior-level design judgment, strong conceptual thinking, and polished work that makes complex ideas understandable.

 - Experience shaping visual direction and delivering projects from early exploration through final production, with substantial hands-on contribution.

 - Strong graphic design fundamentals and experience creating flexible visual systems across digital or physical applications.

 - An experimental practice that includes prototyping, testing approaches, and learning new tools or formats as the idea requires.

 - The curiosity to understand unfamiliar research, ask precise questions, and preserve technical meaning rather than simplify it inaccurately.

 - The ability to guide collaborators, explain design decisions, synthesize feedback, and maintain momentum when a brief is still developing.
