title: EDA Cloud & Developer Infrastructure Engineer
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, our custom silicon program, the team works across silicon architecture, RTL design, verification, physical design, systems software, and infrastructure to deliver highly performant, efficient, and scalable hardware solutions.

The Silicon & Systems team brings together hardware and software engineers to co-design and build the next generation of AI infrastructure. We operate at the intersection of silicon, systems, and software, tackling complex technical challenges across the full hardware development lifecycle, from early architecture and design through validation, deployment, and production.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Infrastructure Software Engineer to build and scale the infrastructure and developer workflows that power OpenAI’s custom silicon development. You’ll work closely with engineering teams across design verification, physical design, emulation, formal verification, and systems software to develop reliable, automated, and efficient workflows that accelerate hardware development.

In this role, you'll own and improve the cloud infrastructure, high-performance computing (HPC) environments, CI/CD pipelines, regression systems, and data platforms that support our silicon engineering teams. You'll translate complex hardware development requirements into scalable infrastructure solutions, reducing manual overhead, improving reliability, and enabling engineers to iterate faster.

This is a highly collaborative, hands-on role with opportunities to drive improvements across the entire hardware development lifecycle. We're looking for engineers who bring deep expertise in one or more infrastructure domains, strong software engineering fundamentals, and an interest in expanding their impact across the broader platform.

In this role, you will:

 - Build developer tools and workflows: Partner with hardware engineering teams to understand their development processes, identify bottlenecks, and build tooling, services, and APIs that automate workflows and accelerate engineering productivity.

 - Develop and scale regression infrastructure: Design, implement, and operate large-scale regression systems spanning job scheduling, execution, results collection, triage, and reporting, with a focus on performance, reliability, and reproducibility.

 - Own CI/CD infrastructure: Build and maintain automated pipelines for infrastructure, developer tooling, and cluster configurations, enabling safe deployments, testing, and continuous improvement.

 - Scale cloud and HPC environments: Design, provision, and operate cloud infrastructure and high-performance compute clusters, optimizing scheduling, capacity, reliability, and cost efficiency to support demanding silicon development workloads.

 - Build data infrastructure and observability: Develop data pipelines, databases, and monitoring systems that provide visibility into regression results, infrastructure health, resource utilization, and engineering efficiency.

 - Drive platform reliability and operational excellence: Troubleshoot complex infrastructure issues, improve monitoring and alerting, automate recovery processes, and build systems that are resilient, maintainable, and scalable.

 - Collaborate across hardware and software teams: Work directly with engineers across RTL, verification, physical design, emulation, and software to continuously improve the infrastructure supporting OpenAI's silicon development.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have strong software engineering fundamentals, with proficiency in Python or a similar programming language and experience building reliable automation, tools, or infrastructure services.

 - Bring deep technical expertise in at least one area of infrastructure engineering, such as Linux/HPC environments, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD systems, storage, networking, or EDA development workflows.

 - Have experience designing, deploying, and operating cloud infrastructure, preferably Azure, with familiarity in infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform or Bicep.

 - Have strong Linux systems knowledge, including processes, filesystems, networking, permissions, performance troubleshooting, and system administration.

 - Have experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines using tools such as Jenkins, Buildkite, GitHub Actions, or similar platforms.

 - Are comfortable debugging complex distributed infrastructure problems, identifying root causes, and implementing durable solutions.

 - Enjoy working closely with engineering teams to understand technical requirements and translate them into scalable, practical infrastructure solutions.

 - Take ownership of systems end to end, from initial design and implementation through deployment, monitoring, and ongoing operational improvements.

 - Bring strong technical judgment, clear communication, and a collaborative approach to solving ambiguous engineering challenges.

 - Are curious about hardware development and excited to expand your technical expertise across infrastructure, silicon design workflows, and developer productivity.

Bonus Qualifications

 - Experience supporting ASIC or semiconductor development environments, including EDA workflows, design verification, physical design, emulation, or formal verification.

 - Experience operating large-scale HPC clusters or workload schedulers such as Slurm.

 - Familiarity with compute farms, regression frameworks, build systems, and hardware development toolchains.

 - Experience with enterprise identity and authentication systems, such as Entra ID, OpenLDAP, FreeIPA, or SSSD.

 - Experience designing and operating relational databases such as PostgreSQL or MySQL, including schema design, migrations, query optimization, and backups.

 - Familiarity with distributed systems components, including message queues, caching layers, artifact storage, and backend services.

 - Experience with high-performance storage systems, data movement optimization, or large-scale compute infrastructure.

 - Experience managing EDA license servers, license utilization, or other shared infrastructure resources in hardware development environments.

title: Engineering Manager, API Multicloud
description:
About the Team

API Multicloud partners with cloud service providers (CSPs) to bring OpenAI’s frontier models and APIs into the cloud environments where developers and enterprises already build. We own the API end to end across CSP platforms, from API integration and request routing through inference execution, capacity management, and day-to-day operations. Our mission is to make these capabilities available broadly and safely while preserving the reliability and developer experience customers expect from OpenAI.

Delivering that experience requires work across the stack: adapting API services and cloud-native integrations, bringing up model-serving environments, validating new releases, and operating the systems that connect customer requests to available capacity. We work directly with CSP engineering teams and partner closely with OpenAI’s inference, API, infrastructure, security, and Safety Systems teams. Together, we turn new model capabilities and partner requirements into dependable production services, with attention to performance, operational readiness, and efficient use of compute.

Our work contributes to OpenAI’s AWS partnership https://openai.com/index/openai-on-aws/, including the launch of Daybreak Red and Daybreak Blue on Amazon Bedrock https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/08/openai-daybreak-red-and-blue-on-amazon-bedrock/ — and OpenAI’s newly announced Google Cloud partnership https://openai.com/index/openai-models-google-cloud/ will bring our frontier models and Codex agentic workflows to Google Cloud’s Model Garden. These efforts let customers use OpenAI capabilities within the cloud infrastructure, security controls, and workflows they already rely on.

About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced Engineering Manager to lead the team responsible for building and operating OpenAI’s API across major cloud service providers. You’ll lead a team of engineers focused on establishing scalable, reliable, and efficient cloud deployment platforms that bring OpenAI’s frontier models to customers across multiple cloud environments.

In this role, you'll own the technical direction, execution, and operational excellence of the API Multicloud platform. You'll guide your team through complex infrastructure challenges, including deploying model-serving environments, scaling capacity, optimizing performance and utilization, and building reusable systems that enable OpenAI to expand across CSP platforms. You'll balance long-term architectural investments with the urgency of delivering new model capabilities and partner integrations.

You'll work closely with engineering leaders across inference, API, infrastructure, security, and Safety Systems, while building strong technical partnerships with CSP engineering teams. Your team will play a critical role in determining how quickly OpenAI can bring new models to market, how reliably those models operate, and how efficiently we scale our infrastructure across cloud providers.

You'll also be responsible for building and developing a high-performing engineering team, setting clear technical priorities, and fostering a culture of ownership, collaboration, and operational excellence.

In this role, you will:

 - Lead, mentor, and grow a high-performing engineering team responsible for building and operating OpenAI's API infrastructure across multiple cloud providers.

 - Define the technical vision, strategy, and roadmap for API Multicloud, ensuring the platform is scalable, reliable, and efficient.

 - Drive the architecture and execution of complex distributed systems that support API routing, model serving, and cloud infrastructure across CSP environments.

 - Partner closely with inference, API, infrastructure, security, and CSP engineering teams to launch new models, expand platform capabilities, and deliver reliable production services.

 - Own the reliability, performance, and operational excellence of the platform, driving improvements in capacity planning, infrastructure efficiency, and deployment processes.

 - Recruit and develop exceptional engineering talent, fostering a culture of technical excellence, ownership, and continuous improvement.

 - Set clear priorities, navigate ambiguity, and drive cross-functional execution while balancing near-term business needs with long-term technical investments.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Experience leading, building, and developing high-performing engineering teams responsible for large-scale cloud infrastructure, distributed systems, or platform engineering.

 - Strong technical background in distributed systems and cloud infrastructure, with the ability to drive architectural decisions and provide technical guidance to senior engineers.

 - Experience building and operating production infrastructure on major cloud platforms such as AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure.

 - Proven track record of leading complex, cross-functional engineering initiatives from architecture through production launch and ongoing operations.

 - Strong understanding of scalability, reliability, performance optimization, and infrastructure efficiency in large-scale production environments.

 - Demonstrated ability to hire, mentor, and develop engineering talent while fostering a culture of technical excellence, ownership, and execution.

About the Team

The Growth team drives user and revenue growth across ChatGPT’s consumer and business segments worldwide. We work across the full funnel, from acquisition and activation to retention and monetization, through product experiments, in-product improvements, performance marketing, creative development, and AI-powered workflows.

The International Growth team works with regional leaders in priority markets to identify the user needs and product gaps that matter most for adoption, usage, and monetization. We turn market priorities into product roadmaps and growth plans, then partner with engineering, research, design, data science, marketing, finance, policy, and partnerships to test and ship improvements.

We combine product strategy with hands-on growth operations. We account for local behavior, competition, and product experience while building shared capabilities such as segmentation, lifecycle journeys, and experimentation systems. We measure what ships, adapt it to the market, and scale approaches that work across markets.

About the Role

We’re looking for a growth lead for Brazil to shape and execute ChatGPT’s growth plans. You’ll partner with regional and market leaders to understand users across Brazil, prioritize the biggest growth opportunities across markets, and turn those priorities into product improvements, funnel optimizations, and performance marketing tests. You’ll work across acquisition, activation, retention, and monetization, collaborating with Product, Engineering, Design, Data Science, Partnerships, and Marketing teams to influence priorities and ship measurable impact. The role combines product growth and funnel optimization with performance marketing: connecting audience, message, creative, and channel learnings to better in-product journeys.

In this role, you will:

 - Partner with regional and market leaders to set a Brazil growth plan and market-level roadmap priorities, with clear hypotheses, owners, dependencies, and measurable outcomes.

 - Use user research, funnel and cohort data, and competitive insight to find local friction and prioritize the opportunities that matter most to users.

 - Run performance marketing tests in collaboration with regional marketers across relevant channels, creators, and partners; use incrementally, CAC, payback, and LTV to decide what to scale.

 - Design and run rigorous experiments across onboarding, activation, repeat usage, re-engagement, and paid conversion; measure incremental impact and iterate. Work with Product, Engineering, Design, and Data Science partners to prototype, test, and ship locally relevant experiences.

 - Partner with regional Marketing and central media teams to brief and prioritize audience, positioning, creative, and channel tests based on the regional plan and market priorities.

 - Own the regional growth scorecard with market-level views across acquisition, retention, paid conversion, and unit economics, distinguishing incremental user and revenue gains and learnings. Connect priority use cases, product improvements, and acquisition plans into a coherent journey from first exposure to repeated value.

 - Run the growth operating cadence with regional and market leaders, aligning central and local partners on results, trade-offs, dependencies, and next steps.

 - Build and operate segmentation, lifecycle journeys, growth tooling, performance marketing and product experimentation capabilities that can be scaled across markets.

You might thrive if you have:

 - 10+ years of experience across product growth, growth marketing, data science, or growth strategy and operations, with hands-on execution in a fast-moving technology company.

 - A user-first track record of turning local research and behavior into product and growth priorities, then shipping improvements with measurable impact.

 - Strong command of acquisition, activation, retention, and monetization funnels, including technically rigorous experimentation and interpretation.

 - Practical performance marketing experience across audience, channel, creative, and measurement decisions, and the ability to partner effectively with media specialists.

 - Analytical fluency in cohort analysis and growth economics, including incrementality, LTV, CAC, payback, and contribution margin.

 - Experience adapting and running campaigns across Latin American markets, using local audience behavior, channels, language, and cultural context to improve relevance and performance at scale.

 - Experience owning growth goals and delivering measurable user or revenue outcomes across product and marketing levers.

 - The ability to influence and align central and regional teams, translate local needs into scalable approaches, and make progress through ambiguity.

 - Become an expert in OAI’s data and systems, through partnership with Data Engineering, Finance, and other Data Science teams.

 - Drive automation of standardized reporting, analysis, and processes across our various revenue segments and compute spend.

title: ML Silicon Performance Lead
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM:

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.


ABOUT THE ROLE:

We’re looking for an ML Silicon Performance Lead to drive hardware/software co-design for our silicon architecture. You will work across models, kernels, compilers, and silicon to shape how ML workloads map to hardware—and how the hardware should evolve to support them. Your work will connect model and workload requirements with compute, memory, and specialized acceleration capabilities to maximize performance, efficiency, and scalability across current and future generations of AI silicon.

You’ll partner closely with ML research, compiler, and silicon architecture teams to jointly develop software approaches and hardware capabilities. From kernel mapping and quantization to new data structures and specialized IP, you’ll evaluate hardware and software tradeoffs to improve performance, efficiency, and utilization across large-scale AI workloads. Through performance modeling, simulation, and hands-on optimization, you’ll guide architectural decisions and validate improvements on representative workloads.


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Drive hardware/software co-design across ML research, compiler, and silicon teams, jointly shaping kernel implementations and hardware capabilities to meet workload performance and efficiency goals.

 - Partner with ML research to translate model and workload needs into kernel performance targets and compute, memory capacity, and bandwidth requirements, feeding hardware constraints and opportunities back into model and algorithm choices.

 - Map and optimize ML kernels for architecture, using insights from data movement, memory hierarchy, and execution efficiency to guide both software improvements and hardware design.

 - Co-design support for new data structures and quantization formats across kernels, compilers, and silicon, balancing model quality, numerical behavior, performance, power, and implementation cost.

 - Define and help develop specialized acceleration IP, working with compiler and silicon partners to determine the right division of functionality across software, instructions, and dedicated hardware.

 - Drive ML performance modeling and simulation with the compiler team to compare hardware/software design options, expose bottlenecks, and quantify end-to-end benefits on representative workloads.

 - Partner with the Silicon Architecture lead and silicon team to specify and validate new IP, using kernel and simulation results to refine requirements and prioritize architectural improvements.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have deep experience with ML accelerator architecture and how compute resources, memory systems, and data movement shape workload performance.

 - Can translate model-level behavior into concrete kernel requirements and hardware design decisions.

 - Have built or used accelerator performance models and simulators, and know how to validate their assumptions and interpret their limitations.

 - Have hands-on experience optimizing ML kernels, including identifying bottlenecks and improving utilization, locality, and execution efficiency.

 - Understand quantization and numerical formats, including their implications for model quality, memory bandwidth, compute efficiency, and hardware support.

 - Have experience with hardware/software co-design and can reason about whether a capability belongs in a kernel, compiler, instruction set, or dedicated hardware.

 - Work effectively across research, compiler, and silicon teams, bringing clarity to ambiguous requirements and building alignment through technical evidence.

description:
About the Team

Financial Engineering (FinEng) builds the financial systems behind ChatGPT, Codex, and OpenAI’s API platform. These products serve people, developers, and businesses around the world. We make them easy to buy, use, and pay for. Our systems support everything from individual subscriptions to usage-based billing and complex enterprise agreements.

We also build the foundations for how products are packaged, accessed, and used: product catalogs, SKUs and bundles, workspaces, entitlements, and usage metering. These systems connect what customers purchase to the capabilities they can access and the usage they can manage.

That reach creates challenging engineering problems. We build services and data pipelines that handle large volumes of usage and transactions, keep payments, product access, and financial records consistent across systems, and adapt as products and pricing change. The same foundations must support a simple checkout and the detailed spending controls a large business needs.

Your work will help teams launch new products faster and give customers confidence in what they are paying for. The work spans customer experiences, backend services, and data systems, with opportunities to influence technical design and see your work through to production.

We’re hiring Staff+ engineers with strong backend experience. Experience in payments, billing, or financial systems is a strong plus, but not required.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and build systems for purchasing, payments, subscriptions, and billing across OpenAI products and global markets.

 - Build product catalogs, SKUs, and bundles that let product teams launch new offerings and evolve how products are packaged.

 - Develop workspace and entitlement systems that connect purchases and subscriptions to product access for individuals and teams.

 - Keep charges and product access correct when requests are retried, updates arrive late, or another service fails.

 - Build metering systems, data pipelines, and APIs that turn large volumes of usage into accurate bills, timely spending information, and records that are easy to trace and verify.

 - Create reusable building blocks that let product teams launch new offerings, pricing, and payment options without rebuilding the foundations each time.

 - Make complex financial workflows simple for customers and internal teams, using customer feedback and experiments to improve the experience.

 - Scale and evolve live systems while protecting customer access, financial accuracy, performance, and security.

 - Own problems from early design through launch and operation, working with product, design, finance, and other engineering teams to make and test important technical decisions.

Nice to Have

 - Experience with payments, subscriptions, pricing, billing, or other systems that manage customer purchases and revenue.

 - Experience with product catalogs, packaging and bundles, workspace management, entitlements, or usage metering.

 - Experience building financial or transaction systems at scale, checking that records match across systems, or supporting compliance and audits.

What You Will Do:
In this role, you will ensure that quality and reliability are designed into our products, components, suppliers, and manufacturing processes from concept through development, launch, ramp, and sustaining operations. You will lead a global team of quality professionals and partner closely with Product Development, Hardware, Software, Reliability, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Customer Experience, and external suppliers.
You will connect customer and field needs to engineering requirements, component controls, supplier capability, manufacturing performance, and product reliability. Your team will help Oura identify risks early, make evidence-based decisions, prevent defects, and resolve complex issues with durable corrective actions.
This is a broad, highly cross-functional leadership role for an experienced quality executive who can set strategy, develop talent, influence engineering and operations leaders, and engage deeply in both product and supply chain quality when needed.
Set the quality strategy: Define Oura’s quality vision, operating model, standards, metrics, and priorities across product development, components, suppliers, manufacturing, reliability, and the field.
Lead and develop a global quality organization: Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing team across product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, and sustaining quality.
Embed quality across the product lifecycle: Establish effective quality gates and decision criteria from concept and architecture through EVT, DVT, PVT, launch, ramp, and sustaining.
Partner with engineering and product leaders: Influence product architecture, design decisions, materials, specifications, interfaces, validation plans, and manufacturability to prevent quality and reliability issues.
Strengthen component and supplier quality: Translate product requirements into component specifications, supplier quality requirements, qualification plans, control plans, inspection strategies, and process controls. Drive supplier capability and performance across the global supply chain.
Drive manufacturing readiness and performance: Ensure production processes are validated and controlled, with appropriate PFMEA, process capability, measurement systems, yield targets, traceability, reaction plans, and continuous improvement mechanisms.
Lead risk-based quality planning: Establish disciplined use of DFMEA, PFMEA, reliability planning, design reviews, tolerance analysis, GR&R, SPC, DOE, and risk-based verification and validation.
Own complex problem solving: Lead containment, failure analysis, root-cause investigation, corrective action, preventive action, and verification of effectiveness for product, component, supplier, manufacturing, reliability, and field issues.
Build strong field-quality feedback loops: Use warranty, returns, customer support, field failure, reliability, manufacturing, and supplier data to identify systemic risks and drive improvements that reduce member impact and cost of poor quality.
Lead launch and ramp readiness: Review product and component qualification, supplier capability, manufacturing readiness, validation evidence, yield, open risks, reliability results, and corrective actions before launch and ramp decisions.
Govern quality-related changes: Ensure design, material, component, supplier, process, software, and manufacturing changes are evaluated for quality and reliability impact and implemented consistently through ECR/ECN and change-control processes.
Establish a data-driven quality operating system: Define leading and lagging indicators across development, suppliers, manufacturing, and the field. Improve data quality, traceability, dashboards, and escalation mechanisms.
Drive continuous improvement: Reduce defects, escapes, returns, warranty claims, rework, scrap, and other sources of cost of poor quality while improving product reliability, supplier performance, and customer experience.
Influence cross-functional decisions: Provide clear, risk-based recommendations when quality, schedule, cost, performance, capacity, and supply continuity priorities compete.
Communicate with senior leadership: Present concise assessments of product risk, supplier and manufacturing performance, launch readiness, field quality, and improvement priorities.
Build a culture of prevention and accountability: Make quality a shared responsibility across engineering and operations, with clear ownership for requirements, validation, supplier controls, manufacturing execution, and sustained performance.
This is a hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.

15+ years of experience in product quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, operations quality, or a related engineering discipline, including significant people leadership experience.
Demonstrated success leading quality for complex, high-volume consumer electronics, wearable, medical-adjacent, or similarly reliability-sensitive products.
Experience leading and developing teams across one or more of the following areas: product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, or sustaining quality.
A track record of establishing quality strategy, operating mechanisms, and measurable improvements from early product development through launch and sustaining.
Strong understanding of product development, design verification and validation, component qualification, reliability engineering, supplier quality, manufacturing processes, and production ramp.
Strong command of quality and problem-solving methods, including FMEA, 8D, CAPA, SPC, GR&R, DOE, root-cause analysis, control plans, and process capability.
Experience using engineering, field, warranty, customer support, supplier, and manufacturing data to identify systemic risks and drive corrective action.
Demonstrated ability to influence engineering, operations, suppliers, and executive leadership without relying solely on direct authority.
Experience with engineering change control, supplier changes, component qualification, process validation, manufacturing readiness, or production quality improvement.
Strong understanding of DFM/DFA, GD&T, Lean and Six Sigma principles, measurement systems, and quality management systems.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical risks into concise decisions and actions.
A self-directed, pragmatic, and resilient leadership style, with a willingness to engage deeply in details while maintaining a strategic perspective.
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, Systems, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field required; advanced degree or quality certification is a plus.

Experience with both product quality and supplier or manufacturing quality, or demonstrated ability to operate effectively across both domains.
Experience with batteries, electronics, sensors, RF systems, precision mechanics, adhesives, miniaturized assemblies, or other demanding product technologies.
Experience leading quality for products that combine hardware, firmware, software, and cloud-enabled member experiences.
Experience building or scaling quality management systems during rapid company growth.
Familiarity with product safety, regulatory, compliance, traceability, and risk-management requirements relevant to wearable technology.
Experience with supplier development, APQP, PPAP, SCAR processes, multi-source strategies, capacity expansion, or major manufacturing transitions.

As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary This position prepares railcars for loading, drives vehicles onto planned railcars, secures vehicles to railcars according to manufacturer and American Association of Railroad standards, and prepares railcars for transportation. Responsibilities Drive new Rivian vehicles onto rail cars Secure vehicles on the rail cars using standard vehicle securement equipment Set bridge plates between railcars for vehicle ingress Position rail loading ramps for proper loading of vehicles Store chocks Inspect vehicles for damage Report damage or mis-bays to Yard Operations leadership Train new employees Other Oubound Yard Logistics duties as assigned Qualifications To be considered for this position, all internal candidates must submit an updated resume highlighting their relevant skills, experiences, and accomplishments. Applications submitted without an updated resume will not be considered. Please ensure that your resume accurately reflects your qualifications for this role. High school diploma or equivalent, preferred. Join Our Team as a Supervisor!
Are you passionate about Leadership ? S&C Electric Company is seeking a dynamic individual to coordinate our Fabrication  function. As a Supervisor , you’ll be crucial in ensuring smooth operations and supporting our diverse team. The Supervisor - Fabrication is responsible for managing the day-to-day operations of the department, leading a team of skilled team members to achieve Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) in safety, quality, delivery, and cost (SQDC). The Supervisor - Fabrication manages CNC and secondary machining equipment and other fabrication operations, ensuring fabricated parts meet quality standards and production timelines. This role requires strong expertise in the assigned area of fabrication, which may include other types of machinery and the ability to inspect and troubleshoot issues in fabrication processes.
Key Responsibilities:
Leadership & People Management: Uphold and promote a professional work environment, addressing minor conflicts and fostering teamwork in line with S&C’s values. Monitor team tasks and provide regular feedback, both constructive and encouraging. Recognize and acknowledge team achievements and guide team members toward growth opportunities through mentoring and coaching .
Department Leadership:  Provide day-to-day leadership support for the department, including supporting all administrative tasks completion, issue resolution, and the seamless coordination of resources. Supervise and guide the team to ensure all job orders and daily metrics are met.
Fabrication Operations: Oversee and guide team members on fabrication processes and workflows, coordinating with department leaders and cascading best practices down to team members through team leads. Ensure team members have the correct training, knowledge, and fabrication equipment to complete their work successfully. Support the planning and coordinating of department production schedules, production rates and capacity plans, processing methods, and times. Review and ensure team understanding of goals and oversee the upkeep of KPI boards.
Quality Management: Conduct inspections of machined parts, finished products or other fabricated materials, ensuring compliance with specifications and initiating corrective actions when needed. Enforce quality control measures to ensure products meet or exceed company standards. Support initiatives to continuously improve product quality and consistency. Set and maintain high levels of product quality. Support communication of corrective action plans, resolutions, and quality results.
Health & Safety Compliance: Promote safety awareness and housekeeping, investigate and report on safety incidents, maintain and promote a safety-conscious manufacturing environment, enforce health and safety policies and procedures to create a safe working environment for all employees, and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and industry standards related to production operations.
Reporting: Create production and status reports. Communicates regularly with upper management regarding problems impacting production. Reports issues regarding production, quality, maintenance, or personnel to function leadership.
Budget Support: Support the Manager in overseeing department’s budget, providing recommendations and helping to review expenditures.
Compliance : Understand and comply with all applicable Company policies and rules
Skills, Knowledge & Experience:
Required
High School Diploma/GED Equivalent
3-5+ years of experience in a leadership role
3-5+ years CNC turning and machining experience knowledge, machining equipment, and fabricating processes.
Good leadership skills within a manufacturing environment, with an ability to lead, guide, motivate, and delegate to deliver results.
Solid critical thinking, organizational, planning, and project management skills, creative problem-solving when obstacles arise.
Good interpersonal skills to establish meaningful relationships built on mutual trust and respect, navigate and resolve conflict, moderate behaviors, and foster collaborative working relationships amongst a diverse audience.
Great communication skills, (written, verbal, listening, and presentation) able to liaise with internal stakeholders from support staff to function leadership.
Adequate financial math skills with the ability to support budgetary decisions.
Good analytical skills with the ability to use and analyze data to drive informed decisions and problem-solve issues.
Proven success partnering across teams, creating effective partnerships at all levels, and collaborating at an operational level.
Adapts to change and different ways of doing things quickly and positively and finds ways to get things accomplished, even when faced with challenges.
Good analytical and problem-solving skills with an ability to leverage data to distil trends and insights that drive continuous improvement.
Proficient computer skills in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook)
Additional Functions:
Maintain regular and punctual attendance
Attend in-person or virtual meetings as requested or required
Communicate effectively and respectfully with others
Other responsibilities as assigned
Preferred
Associate’s degree in a technical discipline, Operations, Engineering, or a related field.
Experience with CNC and secondary machining equipment.
Decision-making capabilities with an ability to make balanced and informed decisions that help S&C achieve business goals
Knowledge of safety regulations and a commitment to maintaining a safe work environment
The ability to work beyond normal working hours according to company needs.
Experience using Oracle HCM

Standing: Occasionally required to stand and perform tasks for up to approximately 2 hours at a time, 5 days per week
Sitting: Frequently required to remain in a stationary position and perform desk-based or production tasks for up to approximately 2 hours at a time, 5 days per week
Walking: Frequently required to walk moderate distances across the S and C campus multiple times per day, 5 days per week
Lifting and Carrying: Infrequently required to solo lift and/or carry items ranging in weight from 5 lbs to 40 lbs,  exercising sound judgement to employ manual handling or machine lifts where required and risk assessments, if appropriate
Low Posture: Infrequently required to perform tasks using a low posture including but not limited to stooping, bending, crawling, crouching, kneeling or squatting
Position Self/ Move: Occasionally required to position self to perform tasks involving but not limited to reaching, twisting, rotating, and pushing/pulling
Manual Dexterity: Occasionally required to use hand-eye coordination to control both hands and arms for a full range of motion to operate equipment/machinery/power tools
Ascending/ Descending: Infrequently ascending or descending ladders and stairs
Observation/ Eyesight: Frequently required to observe details at close range including depth perception, peripheral vision, and the ability to differentiate between colors

Availability: Occasionally required to work extended hours when necessary

Join Our Team as a Chemical Technologist!
The Chemical Technologist will support the Polymer Products process engineering team. The Chemical Technologist performs a variety of material testing associated with cypoxy™  formulations for the purposes of quality assurance and production / engineering support.  The principal responsibilities include performing weekly routine material testing, material testing based on production / engineering needs, writing/creating test reports for routine material testing, assisting with non-conforming and return material authorization analyses, conducting experiments, collecting and analyzing process data, and writing standard work instructions.
Key Responsibilities:
Perform weekly routine material testing associated with cypoxy™ formulations and other raw materials/chemicals used for molding operations – viscosity, density, loss on ignition, glass transition temperature, track testing, hardness, surface roughness, particle size distribution analysis, concentration analysis, etc.
Write/create test reports for the routine material tests performed and communicate the test results with the relevant stakeholders on a weekly basis.
Assist polymer engineering team with Non-Conforming Material Reports (NMR) and Returned Material Authorization (RMA) investigations and test reports.
Conduct experiments, collect and analyze process data using statistical tools, write clear, concise test reports describing the test procedures, results, analyses, and conclusions for any quality related investigations.
Learn about the quality guidelines defined in Inspection Specifications Procedure (ISPs) for all polymer products and become an engineering representative to disposition products that are on-hold for engineering review by Operations team on a timely basis.
Collaborate with operations and polymer engineering team to create instruction bulletins for standard work practices related to tooling/processes.
Collaborate with team members to support the continuous improvement of processes and equipment in the polymer lab.
What you Need to Succeed:
Associate's or bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Polymer Science, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and laboratory experience
1+ years of experience performing material or chemical testing in a laboratory or manufacturing quality environment. Internships, co-ops, and academic lab experience count toward this requirement.
Experience working with polymer materials.
Ability to perform repetitive tasks and run lab equipment associated with routine material testing.
Ability to work with people in a lab and production/plant environment.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Proficiency with PC in using Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Knowledge of safe chemical handling, SDS (Safety Data Sheets) and PPE
Basic record-keeping and documentation, troubleshooting skills, ability to plan and prioritize workloads.
Preferred:
Experience operating laboratory equipment such as Mettler Toledo DSC and Microtrac particle size analyzers
Familiarity with statistical analysis tools such as Minitab or SPC

Observation/Eyesight: Frequently  required to observe details at close range including depth perception, peripheral vision, and the ability to differentiate between colors
Communication: Continuously required to talk and hear, in person and by phone/conference calls
Environmental & Hazardous Conditions
Frequently working indoors/outdoors in an air-conditioned office/manufacturing/site-based environment
Frequently  exposure to fumes/vapors/dust/gases/odors/mist/chemicals/vibration/grease/oils.
Occasionally  exposed to low/moderate/high noise levels including machinery/vehicles/forklifts/office equipment/lab equipment.
Occasionally  working around energized equipment with the risk of electrocution/scalding/burns.
Occasionally  exposed to wet humid/outdoor weather/extreme cold (non-weather)/extreme heat (non-weather) conditions.
Occasionally  working with machinery with moving parts/vehicles/forklifts/heavy machinery/sharp objects.

Lean Six Sigma or similar process-improvement credentials, with automation and AI experience

ABOUT STANDARD BOTS

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next.



ABOUT THE ROLE

*We're hiring a Lead, but if you're a strong functional safety engineer at Senior, Staff or Principal level, we still want to hear from you. We'll level the role and the offer to the person.

If you want a mature process to run, this isn't the role. If you want to build the safety organization behind the best cobot in the world, with the authority to do it, read on.

Standard Bots arms work right next to people, installed by customers who may have never set up a robot before, with no cage and no integrator's risk assessment to lean on. The robot has to be safe by design, and you'll be the one who proves it.

We want to build the best collaborative robot in the world, and that's impossible without building the safest one: a robot anyone can put next to their people on day one and trust. Most of the industry treats safety as paperwork at the end. We want it to be the thing our robots are known for — designed in from the first sketch and proven on real hardware.

Until now, safety has lived inside our hardware, firmware and test teams, like it does at most young companies that ship. That got our first robots out the door. It won't carry what's next: volume growing fast, several new products in development, and AI changing how robots are taught. So we're pulling safety into one strong team with its own mandate — and that team needs a leader.



📍 LOCATION

Glen Cove, New York, is where our robots are built and tested and where the team's center of gravity sits, so this role requires 5 days/week onsite.



WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - The safety case. You own it across our products — analysis, architecture, and the certification plan that gets each robot through third-party assessment.

 - The relationship with assessors. You're our technical voice toward notified bodies and NRTLs, and you're the one in the room defending the argument.

 - Verification on real robots. Every safety function gets tested on hardware you trust, fault injection included. You stay hands-on — this is not a reviewing job.

 - The team. You hire and lead the functional safety engineers who join after you, starting with one who leans electronics and controls and one who leans software.

 - Safety in the design, not at the gate. You report to the Head of System Architecture and work daily with hardware, embedded firmware and test. Safety sits in design reviews from the first sketch.


YOUR FIRST YEAR

 - You've owned a safety case for a shipping robot and defended it to an external assessor.

 - Every safety function has a verification on real hardware that you trust, including fault injection.

 - Your decisions are in the safety architecture of our next generation of arms.

 - Hardware and firmware engineers come to you early, because it saves them time.

 - You've built a team that runs without you in the room, and set how Standard Bots works on safety.



WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - You've taken collaborative robots, or machinery of similar complexity, through third-party safety assessment — and you can tell us what went wrong.

 - You work fluently in ISO 10218-1 and -2, ISO 13849-1 and -2, ISO 12100 and IEC 61508, and you have an opinion on the 2025 revision of ISO 10218.

 - You can read a schematic and a firmware architecture well enough to challenge the engineers who wrote them.

 - You know the full toolkit (FMEA, FTA, HAZOP, STPA, SISTEMA) and which one to reach for.

 - You'd rather be on the test floor with a robot and a force gauge than in a document review.

 - You know the difference between what the standard requires and what actually makes the robot safe, and you deliver both.

 - For the Lead seat: you've led or mentored safety engineers, or you're ready to build a team for the first time.

You don't need to tick every box. If you're close — at any level — apply anyway. We'd rather meet you.

Nice to have

 - You've worked on the assessor side, at a notified body or NRTL.

 - You know mobile manipulators and AMRs: ANSI/RIA R15.08, ISO 3691-4.

 - You've built or specified a safety controller rather than bought one.

 - You've shipped at a startup and liked it.



COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

The salary range for this role is $170,000 - $230,000, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

title: Climate Program Manager
description:
Who we are
About Stripe

About the team
To avoid the worst effects of climate change, most climate models agree the world will need to dramatically reduce emissions and remove 5-10 billion tons of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere per year by 2050. The Climate team’s goal is to accelerate Stripe’s path to net zero in parallel with the world’s. We do this by reducing Stripe’s emissions and leading initiatives to increase the likelihood that we have the global carbon removal capacity necessary to reach these climate goals.
In 2019, we developed the first measurement of Stripe’s enterprise emissions. In 2021 we launched Stripe Climate , enabling merchants to direct a fraction of their revenue to help scale emerging carbon removal technologies. In 2022 we launched Frontier , an advance market commitment to buy $1.8B+ of permanent carbon removal by 2040. In 2024, we entered our first multi-year offtake for clean energy.
Today, Stripe’s corporate net zero program is entering a new phase. We are looking to streamline our emissions measurement, create a template for catalytic emission reduction and champion buying removals on the path to net zero, all while meeting our expanding global ESG disclosure requirements.
What you’ll do
As Stripe’s Climate Program Manager, you will set the strategy and lead the execution and reporting for Stripe’s corporate net zero program. You’ll partner with a wide range of stakeholders within and outside of Stripe – Accounting, Finance, Legal, Procurement, Facilities, Sales, and carbon accounting and assurance providers – to refine our greenhouse gas inventory, deliver a reduction and removal roadmap that meets our climate targets, and provide inputs to global ESG disclosures.
This role requires someone with expertise in carbon accounting and reductions strategy, sharp program and process management, a track record of getting big things done fast, and excellent judgement to make the ‘right’ recommendations for Stripe’s net zero program.
Responsibilities
Net Zero strategy (~15%): Own and evolve Stripe’s corporate net zero strategy, including Stripe’s transition plan, priorities, budget, annual goals, emissions forecasts, removal retirements, and progress tracking. Stay current on evolving disclosure requirements, net zero guidance, and industry best practices to ensure Stripe’s program is high impact and best in class
Emissions measurement (~30%): Build Stripe’s annual greenhouse gas inventory. Collect data inputs, evolve methodology, manage Stripe’s footprint vendors, run a rigorous and auditable process with cross-functional stakeholders, and identify opportunities to use AI to improve the accuracy and efficiency of this process
Emissions reporting (~30%):  Serve as Stripe’s subject-matter expert to deliver inputs to ESG controllership for regulatory disclosures and clear recommendations for executives and customers
Reduction program (~25%): Develop and manage emissions reduction initiatives across Stripe. This will include efforts like securing renewable electricity for Stripe’s scope 2 emissions, as well as driving creative and high-impact interventions like carbon removal or lower-emission data centers that we need to reach global net zero

Minimum requirements
BA or BS degree
5-7+ years of experience in corporate sustainability, climate strategy, carbon accounting, environmental consulting, or a related field
Excellent oral and written communication skills – especially adept at translating complexity into clear recommendations
A track record of generating and implementing ambitious emissions reduction initiatives
Strong quantitative skills and expertise in emissions accounting and Greenhouse Gas Protocol
Preferred qualifications
Has led a corporate climate program in a sector with a significant Scope 3 footprint, ideally technology or financial services
Is a self-starter, and has a proven track record of translating climate ambitions into actionable plans and producing measurable reductions through clean energy, cloud usage, and other supplier engagement initiatives

Has experience partnering with cross functional controllership partners to manage a greenhouse gas inventory process that meets requirements for limited or reasonable assurance
Is an exceptionally fast learner. Enjoys (and has experience) quickly ramping on new reduction technologies and sustainability standards

Infrastructure at Privy is fundamentally a product. Build a supportive, fun, motivating, celebratory team culture so that the team wins every week

Performance-oriented mindset, with a high bar for quality and excellence
